Article Title: 'Debate in Parliament': Himanta Sarma hits back at Rahul Gandhi's challenge to PM Modi
Article Text:
Himanta Sarma responds to Rahul Gandhi’s challenge to Modi

Sarma cites Bofors, Bhopal gas tragedy

Rahul Gandhi challenges PM Modi to public debate

NEW DELHI: Assam chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma on Wednesday responded to Congress leader and leader of the opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi's challenge to Prime Minister Narendra Modi for a public debate, saying the discussion should take place in Parliament rather than on the streets.In a post on X, Sarma took a swipe at the Rae Bareli MP over his Diwali greeting to the Prime Minister, in which the Congress leader had wished Modi on the festival while holding a rose.“Dear Rahul ji, roses are given on Valentine’s Day, not on Diwali. Anyway, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) will see you in Parliament,” Sarma wrote.In a video shared on X, the Assam chief minister questioned whether Rahul was aware of his responsibilities as the leader of the opposition and said Parliament was the appropriate venue for a debate with the Prime Minister.“Rahul ji, yesterday you posted a video. You were holding a rose and wishing the Prime Minister a Happy Diwali. Rahul ji, roses are given on Valentine’s Day; they are not given on Diwali. Tell me one thing: are you even aware that you are the Leader of the Opposition? If you are the Leader of the Opposition and if you truly consider yourself to be one, then where is this debate with the Prime Minister supposed to take place? On the streets? In some alleyway? Or in Parliament?” Sarma said.He also referred to the presence of the Lok Sabha Speaker and members of Rahul's family in Parliament, arguing that the debate could be held there.Sarma said several issues, including the Bofors controversy and the Bhopal Gas Tragedy, could be taken up during a parliamentary debate. He urged former Congress president to initiate the discussion and ensure that proceedings were not disrupted.“There are plenty of issues to discuss, from Bofors to the Bhopal Gas Tragedy. This time, please ensure there is no ruckus in Parliament. You should initiate the debate; the Prime Minister will respond, and all these issues can be addressed,” he said.Questioning the Congress leader's call for a public face-off outside Parliament, Sarma added, “Why do you want to drag people out onto the streets? This isn't Bangladesh; this isn't Nepal. Rahul ji, do not take the people for fools.”He further advised the Congress leader to move away from what he described as the role of an “angry young man” and participate in a peaceful debate in Parliament.The Congress MP had issued the challenge in a post on X on Tuesday, urging PM Modi to agree to a public debate in the presence of the media and the country's youth.“It’s been 24 hours since I challenged you, Modi ji. You say the opposition is anti-national. Choose any stage, any venue, and debate me on this - Who is anti-national? Who has connections with foreign forces? And what is the nature of those connections? Let’s do this as soon as possible. Daro mat!” Rahul wrote.Proposing a format for the discussion, the Congress leader said both leaders could sit across a table, with the Prime Minister free to appoint the moderator.“We’ll both be there. The media will be there. The youth of this country will be there. There will be a table. You’ll sit on one side, I’ll sit on the other. You can appoint whoever you want as the judge. You can even make Mohan Bhagwat ji the judge,” he said.Rahul also listed several issues he wanted to raise, including the financial system, the India-US deal, the Adani case and the Epstein matter.“There will be questions about the financial system, the financial structure, how the US deal happened, why it happened and why so quickly, why you made the deal alone and didn’t inform the Cabinet, why the Adani case was closed, Epstein - and many other issues. We’ll discuss all of them openly.Let the truth come out. Let everything be crystal clear,” he added.The Congress leader also challenged PM Modi to file a defamation case against him over his allegations, saying he was already facing several such cases.“You make allegations against me, don’t you? Come forward. Everything will become clear. You’ve filed defamation cases against me over other matters. I think there are around 45 defamation cases against me. But on this issue of the debate, on the question of foreign connections, you haven’t filed a defamation case. Go ahead, file one. We’ll discuss that openly too. Happy Diwali, Modi ji,” Rahul wrote.
Article Summary: Assam chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma responds to Rahul Gandhi's challenge to PM Modi for a public debate. Sarma questions whether Rahul is aware of his responsibilities as the leader of the opposition. He says Parliament is the appropriate venue for a debate with the Prime Minister.

Article Title: One more Indian seafarer killed near Oman; toll 23
Article Text:
Indian seafarer Gandhar Nahim Ajij from Gujarat killed after a vessel was struck by an unidentified aerial object near Oman, taking the number of Indians killed in the West Asia conflict to 23

NEW DELHI: An Indian seafarer died in an attack on a commercial vessel near Oman, taking the toll of Indian nationals killed in the West Asia conflict to 23. Of these 23 Indians, 15 were seafarers.India condemned the attack on MSV AL JUSUFI near Limah in Oman. On Tuesday, shipping minister Sarbananda Sonowal on X said on Nov 2 (Monday), the Indian vessel carrying 14 Indian seafarers was struck by an unidentified aerial object while navigating near the Oman coast. "While 13 crew members safely evacuated and were rescued by Omani Coast Guard, I am deeply saddened to report that one of our seafarers, Gandhar Nahim Ajij from Gujarat, tragically succumbed to injuries," he said.In a statement, MEA said the continuing attacks on commercial shipping in the region are deeply concerning and reiterated India’s call for immediate deescalation of tensions, and the conclusion of ongoing negotiations for a diplomatic solution so that peace and stability can return to the region. “The targeting of commercial shipping and civilian infrastructure in the region must end, and free and unimpeded navigation and commerce through the international waterways in the region, in keeping with international law, must be restored at the earliest,” it said.Responding to a question on Russia-Ukraine conflict, also said that five Indians had been killed so far in attacks in the Black Sea region. Officials said that so far, 4,330 Indian sailors have been brought back safely from the conflict-hit Persian Gulf. They added that currently there are eight Indian-flagged ships in the Persian Gulf and six of them are operating in that region.“Two foreign-flagged ships carrying fertilisers are waiting to transit through the Strait of Hormuz,” said an official.
Article Summary: An Indian seafarer died in an attack on a commercial vessel near Oman, taking the toll of Indian nationals killed in the West Asia conflict to 23. Of these 23 Indians, 15 were seafarers. Officials said that so far, 4,330 Indian sailors have been brought back safely from the conflict-hit Persian Gulf.

Article Title: Indian tourist killed, PIO injured as copters collide during Everest rescue
Article Text:
Indian killed as copters collide during Everest rescue

Here's what happened

(With agency inputs)

A 47-year-old tourist from Chennai was killed and two others - an Indian-origin New Zealand citizen and a pilot - were injured when two helicopters collided barely about 10 feet above a helipad near Mt Everest on Tuesday. The accident occurred around 8.11am at Pheriche, 12km south of Everest Base Camp, as one helicopter was evacuating tourists stranded by heavy snowfall and the other was carrying cargo.The rotor blades of the two choppers struck each other as both aircraft attempted to land, sending them crashing onto the snow-covered helipad. Aviation authorities suspect miscommunication between the pilots, who were operating beyond the coverage of the nearest air traffic control tower in Lukla - gateway to the Everest region. The accident is believed to be Nepal's first mid-air collision involving two helicopters.The deceased was identified as Vasanth Kumar Balaramudu, who died at the scene. Shailesh Krishna Patel (49), a New Zealand citizen, and Fishtail Air pilot Rabindra Prajapati sustained injuries. Balaramudu and Patel were being evacuated aboard a private Fishtail Air Airbus AS350 helicopter, registration 9N-AJR, which had taken off from Gorakshep, a remote settlement near Everest Base Camp at an altitude of approximately 5,164 metres.The other helicopter, an Air Dynasty AS350 registered 9N-AOD, had flown from Lukla carrying cargo. Its pilot, the sole occupant, escaped unhurt. Verified footage showed the helicopters approaching the helipad from different directions, with one descending faster than the other.The weather appeared clear, with no visible signs of strong winds. People nearby rushed towards the wreckage immediately after the collision. “Preliminary reports suggest miscommunication between the pilots, as the area is outside the coverage of Lukla Airport’s air traffic control tower and pilots have to communicate with each other,” said Mukesh Dangol, director general of the Civil Aviation Authority of Nepal.“We are recording the statement of the injured pilot,” he added. CAAN spokesperson Gyanendra Bhul said, “It appears the accident happened when two helicopters attempted to land at the same spot.” The aviation authority has launched an investigation to establish how both aircraft came to approach the helipad simultaneously. Solukhumbu district official Kaman Singh Thapa Magar also confirmed that the weather was clear at the time but raised the possibility of a technical problem.Prajapati and Patel were flown by a Prabhu Air helicopter to Nepal Mediciti Hospital in Kathmandu Valley.Air Dynasty confirmed that its pilot was uninjured, contradicting initial reports that both pilots had sustained injuries. Balaramudu’s body was first taken to Lukla and later transported to Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital in Kathmandu for a post-mortem before repatriation to India.India’s foreign ministry said the Indian embassy in Kathmandu was coordinating with Nepalese authorities to bring back Balaramudu’s remains. Pheriche, at around 4,300 metres, is a key stop along the Everest trekking route. Heavy snowfall had disrupted trails and left tourists stranded at high-altitude settlements, including Gorakshep, prompting helicopter evacuations. Expeditions are under way on Everest and nearby Ama Dablam.With no road access to the upper Everest region, choppers are widely used to ferry climbers and supplies, besides carrying out rescues.
Article Summary: Vasanth Kumar Balaramudu, 47, died at the scene. Shailesh Krishna Patel (49), a New Zealand citizen and Fishtail Air pilot Rabindra Prajapati sustained injuries. Aviation authorities suspect miscommunication between the pilots, who were operating beyond the coverage of the nearest air traffic control tower.

Article Title: Major fire breaks out at HPCL Visakhapatnam refinery, no casualties
Article Text:
A fire occurred at Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited Visakh Refinery during the night, alarming nearby residents.





VISAKHAPATNAM: A fire that broke out at Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited's (HPCL) Visakhapatnam refinery in Malkapuram on Monday night was brought under control, with no casualties or injuries reported.The fire was confined to a pitch intermediate storage tank in the refinery's sulfur unit, and all units at the facility are operating safely, HPCL said.In a post on X, the company said the fire was reported around 10pm on November 2, following which its Fire and Safety Team immediately activated firefighting and emergency response measures."The fire was localised to the pitch tank area and was brought under control within a short time. There have been no casualties," HPCL said, adding that all refinery units were functioning safely.Malkapuram Circle Inspector E Narasimha Rao said the fire involved sulfur pitch, a waste or bottom product generated in the refinery's sulfur unit. He said HPCL's own fire tenders were deployed to tackle the blaze and no external assistance was required."There are no casualties, no injuries and no major issues. Everyone is safe, and there is no need for panic," he said.Revenue Divisional Officer (RDO) Dileep Chakravarthy, who visited the site, said the fire had been completely extinguished using the firefighting equipment installed at the refinery and resources deployed by the Andhra Pradesh Fire Department.He said a small blast was reported at the facility before the fire broke out. Chakravarthy added that an enquiry would be initiated to examine industrial safety at the facility in accordance with applicable norms."There is no cause for worry, and no injuries or casualties have been reported. People are requested not to panic about the incident," he said.Meanwhile, eyewitnesses said the flames rising from the refinery were large enough to frighten people in the vicinity. One eyewitness said people moved away from the area after seeing the blaze.
Article Summary: A fire broke out at Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited's (HPCL) Visakhapatnam refinery on Monday night. No casualties or injuries were reported. The fire was confined to a pitch intermediate storage tank in the refinery's sulfur unit.

Article Title: Sonam Wangchuk’s wife told to stop classes in Leh school

Ladakh authorities ask Sonam Wangchuk-founded HIAL to halt school activities in Leh pending HC decision on land dispute

SRINAGAR: Ladakh Union territory (UT) authorities have directed Himalayan Institute of Alternatives (HIAL), founded by climate activist Sonam Wangchuk , to refrain from starting classes and other activities at a school within the complex in Leh till a land dispute pending in the high court is decided.A notice pertaining to Desert Flower School was issued to Gitanjali J. Angmo, Wangchuk’s wife who is listed as HIAL’s official founder and CEO. The notice says moves to start classes at the school could “prejudice” proceedings pending in the HC.“The notice takes serious note of the reported commencement of school activities without obtaining requisite consent, clearances and approvals from the concerned authorities,” a govt spokesperson said in a statement.The school was preparing to begin its new academic session, for which it had sought an NOC that has not been granted so far, sources said. Gitanjali dismissed the notice as “baseless”, claimed a reply had been sent and blamed the authorities for the delay in the NOC.According to the govt spokesperson, the notice issued by the Leh tehsildar advises HIAL to maintain “strict status quo” and “not undertake any action whatsoever towards functioning or commencement of activities at the school” until the final HC decision.Ladakh authorities had cancelled HIAL’s land allotment in Aug 2025, following which it moved the HC. In an affidavit last month, the authorities accused HIAL of occupying the land without paying dues. The affidavit also accused Wangchuk of inciting violence in Leh in Sept last year in which four people were killed and scores injured in alleged police firing on protesters demanding statehood and Sixth Schedule status for Ladakh.Wangchuk is also a member of Leh Apex Body (LAB), one of the organisations spearheading the demands and holding talks with the Centre on autonomy.
Article Summary: Ladakh authorities ask Sonam Wangchuk-founded HIAL to halt school activities in Leh pending HC decision on land dispute. The notice says moves to start classes at the school could ‘prejudice’ proceedings pending in the HC.

Article Title: 'Radical thinking': INDIA bloc allies snub Left leader Neha Bora's 'Brahmanvaad' remark
Article Text:
Neha Bora at a press conference at the CPI(ML) Liberation Parliamentary Office in New Delhi.

NEW DELHI: Congress's key ally, Samajwadi Party , has unequivocally distanced itself from the "Brahmanvaad" remark of Left-wing student leader Neha Bora.The AISA president, under the patronage of INDIA bloc leaders, gained limelight for fiercely criticising the poll body chief Gyanesh Kumar and the electoral roll purge under the Special Intensive Revision (SIR).On Bora's "need freedom from Brahmanvaad" remark, Samajwadi Party's Rajeev Rai said: "Making such a sweeping statement is not appropriate. Every religion has both good and bad people; we shouldn't make such generalisations... We should avoid them. That is exactly what the BJP wants; why should we fall into their trap?"Rai, who represents the Ghosi Lok Sabha constituency in poll-bound Uttar Pradesh, firmly repudiated the AISA leader's rhetoric riddled with "sweeping generalisations"."In this day and age, the kind of rhetoric being used is simply unacceptable. There is no basis for it. We shouldn't make sweeping generalisations about any caste, community, religion, or region," he said.Akhilesh Yadav's party is not the only one to shrug off Bora's statement, as Uddhav Sena leader Priyanka Chaturvedi also called her assertions "unfortunate", saying radical thinking, be it from the Right or the Left, is harmful to the nation."It is highly unfortunate. While I believe this may be an old video, it reveals a mindset that asserts rapes happen in temples, are committed by priests, and that Brahmin women are unsafe. I generally avoid focusing on caste, but as a Brahmin woman myself, I must ask: is it appropriate to use such derogatory language? I have always maintained that this kind of radical thinking—whether from the Left or the Right—is harmful to the nation," the former Rajya Sabha member said.She, however, said she would like to "sit down with Neha Bora and explain that not everything should be viewed through the lens of caste or religion"."She is young, talented, bright, and smart, with the drive to fight for a cause; she ought to use her intellect more constructively," Chaturvedi said.Earlier, the BJP targeted Bora over a video showing her criticising the “Brahmanical system”, with party spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari accusing her of spreading “Hindu hate”.Sharing the video on X, Bhandari called Bora the “poster girl” of what he described as Rahul Gandhi’s anti-Hindu politics.In the video, Bora is heard speaking about women's safety and criticising the Brahmanical system. She reportedly referred to the Unnao and Kathua cases while making her remarks.Bhandari also linked her comments to an earlier statement by Rahul Gandhi on the safety of women."Neha Bora poster girl of Rahul Gandhi displays her Hindu hate," Bhandari wrote.He added, "She is inspired from Rahul Gandhi who earlier had said 'Mandiro main ladkiyon ke sath ched chad hoti hai'.""Congress Hates Hindus, loves vote bank! Congress Soch is a threat to India's unity!" Bhandari posted.The remarks triggered a political row after the video surfaced on social media. However, the clip is undated, and the circumstances in which Bora made the comments could not be independently verified.Bora has been actively involved in protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.She took part in an October 10 demonstration organised by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and student groups in Delhi. Police detained several protesters, including Bora, as restrictions on public gatherings were imposed in parts of the capital.The AISA president also backed the INDIA bloc's November 1 rally against the CEC, urging people to join the opposition's demonstration in Delhi.She has also appeared alongside Rahul Gandhi and other opposition leaders during protests against the poll body chief. Bora was also present at "mock" Parliament which was organised to symbolically "impeach" Gyanesh Kumar.
Article Summary: Samajwadi Party's Rajeev Rai said: "Making such a sweeping statement is not appropriate" Uddhav Sena leader Priyanka Chaturvedi called her assertions "unfortunate" Bora has been actively involved in protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

Article Title: 'Deeply touched': PM Modi thanks Bhutan King for dedicating sacred stupa in his honour
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday expressed gratitude to Bhutan's King Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuck after a sacred Buddhist stupa was dedicated to him in Gelephu Mindfulness City, Bhutan.In a social media post, PM Modi said he was "deeply touched" by the special gesture of warmth and generosity shown by the King and the people of Bhutan, adding that he accepted the honour with gratitude on behalf of the people of India.He described the Jangchub Chorten as an enduring symbol of the shared spiritual and civilisational heritage and friendship between the two countries.In a separate social media post, the Bhutanese King said the 76th Stupa was dedicated to Prime Minister Modi on November 1, after 108 stupas were raised in Gelephu Mindfulness City.King Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuck, along with India's Union minister for parliamentary affairs Kiren Rijiju, unveiled a plaque dedicating the stupa to Modi.The King said the dedication was an enduring symbol of his "profound appreciation" for PM Modi's unwavering commitment and India's steadfast support for the realisation of his vision for Gelephu Mindfulness City.The 108 Jangchub Chortens form part of Bhutan's effort to highlight its Buddhist heritage and spiritual identity through the Gelephu Mindfulness City project.The dedication of the 76th stupa to PM Modi adds a diplomatic dimension to the initiative, reflecting the close relationship between the two neighbouring countries. The gesture also underscores Bhutan's appreciation of India's support for its development ambitions and the enduring cultural and spiritual links between the two nations.
Article Summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi expressed gratitude to Bhutan's King Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuck. A sacred Buddhist stupa was dedicated to him in Gelephu Mindfulness City, Bhutan. PM Modi said he was "deeply touched" by the special gesture of warmth and generosity shown by the King.

Article Title: Bihar CM Samrat Chaudhary says ‘crime might happen, but not apradh’; Tejashwi takes swipe

NEW DELHI: Bihar chief minister Samrat Chaudhary on Tuesday courted criticism after claiming that "crime might happen in the state, but not apradh (which also means crime in Hindi)" - a remark that opposition leader Tejashwi Yadav seized on to mock him.Choudhary made the remark while addressing an event marking an agreement between the Union ministry of road transport and highways and the Bihar government on river water management."There is no apradh here. The concept of apradh has ended. Crime may happen, but not apradh. There are no criminals," he reportedly said.Reacting to the statement, Tejashwi questioned the IAS and IPS officers present on the stage with the chief minister, asking whether they felt "honoured or humiliated" to work with him."In Bihar, 'crime' may happen, but not 'apradh'! My dear fellow countrymen, this is being said by a sample accused in seven murders, the chief minister selected by Modi ji. Do the IAS/IPS officers sitting on the stage feel honoured or humiliated to be working with these people?" Tejashwi said in a post on X."Has Narendra Modi ji taken a contract to ruin Bihar through this man?" he added.Choudhary also spoke about Bihar's development and industrial growth, saying the state had lost 87% of its revenue to Jharkhand after the latter was carved out of Bihar.He said the government had decided to restart mining operations and ensure supplies within 30 days of an order. He identified population and water as Bihar's two biggest weaknesses.Referring to the agreement being signed under the leadership of Union road transport and highways minister Nitin Gadkari, Choudhary said effective management of river water could help Bihar overcome its challenges. He added that if the state managed its river resources properly, "the fear would be 100% over".
Article Summary: Bihar chief minister Samrat Chaudhary courted criticism after claiming that "crime might happen in the state, but not apradh" Opposition leader Tejashwi Yadav seized on the remark to mock him. Choudhary made the remark while addressing an event marking an agreement.

Article Title: SC to define right to privacy of protesters in public places
Article Text:
SC agrees to examine privacy rights of protesters amid concerns over Delhi Police’s use of CCTV cameras and facial recognition technology

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Tuesday agreed to examine the contours of right to privacy of people when they are part of a public protest as lawyers appearing for recent protesters in the capital claimed breach of privacy because of the deployment of CCTV cameras and facial recognition tools by Delhi Police.Appearing for a petitioner, political activist and advocate Prashant Bhushan told a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that deployment of facial recognition tools as well as CCTV cameras, and the use of data generated by them required scrutiny so that they were not put in the public domain or used for harassing young protesters.Solicitor-general Tushar Mehta said CCTV cameras were installed for the safety of protesters. He added that fears of anti-social and criminal elements mingling with protesters to cause damage to public property and resort to violence came true during CJP's "illegal" July 20 march to Parliament call. "It was primarily to ensure the safety of women," he said.Justice Bagchi said CCTV surveillance may not per se violate the right to privacy but if that data was fed into a machine for facial identification and tracing history of an individual, then it may amount to breach of privacy."It has to be examined whether this action infracts privacy," he added.Senior advocate Mahesh Jethmalani interjected and said the court was only determining the constitutional rights of protesters. What about the rights of innocent citizens whose daily lives and livelihoods got derailed by these protests, he asked and suggested that the court devise an SOP for protests to fasten liability on the organisers for loss and damage to public property and loss of livelihood.The SC said the Identification of Prisoners Act, replaced by the Criminal Procedure (Identification) Act, 2022, empowers the state to identify people by using iris data and those provisions need to be kept in mind. The SG said though the case did not involve prisoners, the law does empower govt to collect data for interests of the state.Justice Bagchi said, "When a person stands in a public place, what is his reasonable expectation?" The SG replied, "One cannot choose to protest in a public place and seek protection of privacy."When Justice Bagchi said it was a competing right - right to privacy and legitimate state interest - Mehta said it was strange that protesters had no problem with scores of live TV channels broadcasting them or swarms of influencers making reels and uploading them on social media but had a problem with govt's CCTVs.Mehta said no iris verification of protesters was ever done by police. The bench said police had said they had matched the IDs of people with NCRB database of criminals. "Does that amount to a legitimate state interest?" it asked. Mehta said after facial recognition, the person concerned with a criminal track record was investigated and called for inquiry.The bench issued a notice on Bhushan's petition and tagged it with petitions questioning deployment of facial recognition tools .
Article Summary: Supreme Court agrees to examine the contours of right to privacy of people when they are part of a public protest. Lawyers appearing for recent protesters in the capital claimed breach of privacy because of the deployment of CCTV cameras and facial recognition tools. Solicitor-general Tushar Mehta said CCTV cameras were installed for the safety of protesters.

Article Title: ‘You remember neither promises nor skullcap’: NCP MP Aga Ruhullah quits, takes aim at Omar Abdullah
Article Text:
Aga Ruhullah Mehdi resigns from National Conference after 24 years, accuses Omar Abdullah of betraying party promises

BUDGAM: Aga Ruhullah Mehdi ended Monday his 24-year association with National Conference, resigning as its functionary and Srinagar MP while declaring his exit an act of “azadi” and accusing CM Omar Abdullah of betraying the party’s election promises, surrendering to BJP and failing to defend J&K’s political rights.Recalling the 2024 assembly election campaign in Ganderbal, Mehdi said Omar had removed his skullcap and sought votes in the name of its dignity. “You remember nothing, neither your promises nor your skullcap,” he said.He handed over the resignation to Muhammad Ashraf Mattoo, father of Tufail Mattoo, who was killed in alleged police firing in 2010 during Omar Abdullah’s tenure as CM, asking him to deliver it to NC president Dr Farooq Abdullah.Farooq had told Mehdi in Aug that he was free to quit. Mehdi announced that he would resign on the death anniversary of his father Aga Syed Mehdi, a Shia cleric and Congress politician assassinated in a terrorist attack on Nov 3, 2000.In an hour-long speech, Mehdi repeatedly called Omar “incompetent” and “meek”, accusing him of being aggressive towards his own people while remaining submissive to BJP. He cited govt’s handling of the reservation policy, the unfulfilled promise of 200 units of free electricity and its failure to mount a forceful demand for restoration of Article 370 Mehdi said he had repeatedly raised these issues within the party over the past two years but was asked by colleagues to remain silent.He accused the CM of meekly pleading with Centre for restoration of statehood and also alleged that Omar had failed to raise the cases of hundreds of youths “who are in jails without trial”.Mehdi indicated plans to float a new party based on “principles and having character”, saying he would travel across J&K to find “suitable people”. He is likely to contest the Srinagar seat as an independent candidate during bypolls.BJP national vice president Ram Madhav distanced his party from NC’s internal developments during a day-long visit to Jammu. “We have no involvement in the internal affairs of National Conference. That is their internal affair. What do we have to do with it?” he said, adding that NC was “visibly divided”.
Article Summary: Aga Ruhullah Mehdi resigns from National Conference after 24 years. Accuses Omar Abdullah of betraying party promises. Mehdi indicated plans to float a new party based on ‘principles and having character’ He is likely to contest the Srinagar seat as an independent candidate during bypolls.

Article Title: EC allows voters deleted from draft electoral rolls to use Form 6 for re-inclusion
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Election Commission on Tuesday allowed previously enrolled voters whose names were deleted from the draft electoral rolls during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) to submit Form 6 to seek their inclusion in the final list.In a letter to all state chief electoral officers, the poll body said it had received reports that some voters were hesitant to submit Form 6. The EC said that voters were concerned about requiring to declare that their names are being included in the electoral rolls for the first time."Therefore, such electors believe that submission of Form 6, in view of their previous enrolment, would amount to making a false declaration and render them liable for prosecution under Section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950," it said.The EC's clarification comes days after the Supreme Court said that no one would be prosecuted for using Form 6 to get their names included in the electoral rolls again.The observation was made by a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohan while hearing a PIL challenging the large-scale exclusion of names from Maharashtra's draft electoral roll. The bench was responding to senior advocate Aravind Datar's submission that using Form 6 for re-inclusion would amount to making a false declaration under oath.“No one will be prosecuted for filling Form 6 seeking re-entering of their names in voter lists," the CJI said.The bench also said, “If we find, even after the publication of the final electoral roll, that there are people who are genuine voters but still excluded, we can extend time for them to submit documents for the purpose of re-entering their names in voter lists.”What is Form 6?Form 6 is the application through which an eligible person seeks inclusion of their name in the electoral roll. According to the Election Commission's guidelines, the application is addressed to the Electoral Registration Officer of the constituency where the applicant ordinarily resides.The form requires basic details such as the applicant's name, details of a relative, Aadhaar information, gender, date of birth and present ordinary residence. Applicants are also required to complete a declaration. The guidelines warn that making a false statement in the declaration is punishable under Section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950.
Article Summary: Election Commission on Tuesday allowed previously enrolled voters whose names were deleted from the draft electoral rolls to submit Form 6. The poll body said it had received reports that some voters were hesitant to submit the form. The EC said that voters were concerned about requiring to declare that their names are being included in the electoral rolls for the first time.

Article Title: Dhirendra Shastri apologises for 'your Krishna, our Ram' remark; controversy explained

Dhirendra Krishna Shastri said he had no intention of insulting any deity.

NEW DELHI: Bageshwar Dham head priest Dhirendra Krishna Shastri apologised after his flippant and ill-considered comparison of Lord Ram and Lord Krishna, deities widely believed to be identical divine forms in Hinduism.In a video message posted on social media from Nairobi, Kenya, Shastri on Monday said he had no intention of insulting any deity or suggesting that one was superior to the other. He apologised to anyone whose religious sentiments may have been hurt by his comments.The controversy began during a recent Ram Katha in Karera in Madhya Pradesh's Shivpuri district.While speaking about the different forms of Lord Ram and Lord Krishna, Dhirendra Krishna Shastri said Ram stands straight, while Krishna stands bent at three places.He was referring to Lord Krishna's 'tribhanga' posture, in which the body is bent at three points, as well as his flute and association with Vrindavan. Shastri also drew a comparison between Ayodhya, associated with Lord Ram, and Vrindavan, associated with Lord Krishna.A video of the remarks subsequently circulated on social media, prompting objections from seers and devotees in Mathura and Vrindavan. They argued that both deities are equally revered and that comparing them in a manner that suggests one is greater than the other was inappropriate.Responding to the criticism, Shastri said his remarks were made in the context of the devotional traditions and expressions of love associated with Braj, the region linked to Lord Krishna.Shastri, describing himself as a devotee of Lord Krishna, said he also narrates the Bhagavad Katha and has complete faith in Krishna devotion.He added that if anyone had been hurt by his emotional remarks, he offered a humble apology.Responding to Shastri's off-the-cuff remark, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav demanded action against the preacher without naming Shastri directly.In a post on X, accompanied by a video of Lord Krishna wielding the Sudarshan Chakra, Yadav described the alleged remarks as "extremely unfortunate and objectionable".He questioned the reasoning behind comparing the two deities in a way that appeared to place one above the other."Both the protector of the people and the one who brings them joy are incarnations of the same divine entity. What is the rationale behind such undignified comparisons? This must be clarified," he said.Yadav alleged that the remarks "appeared to reflect the designs of someone working behind the scenes" and warned that "failure to check such statements could create an atmosphere of discord and resentment in society".He said followers of Sanatan traditions revered both Lord Ram and Lord Krishna and that the remarks had hurt members of the community as well as people from other faiths.The SP chief also urged those claiming to represent Sanatan traditions to speak out against such comments, saying people across political parties had united in opposing them."Any kind of venomous expression against any religion, faith, sect or its revered deities and great figures is absolutely unacceptable. The matter should be taken up at the highest level, and punitive action should be taken," the former Uttar Pradesh CM said.
Article Summary: Bageshwar Dham head priest Dhirendra Krishna Shastri apologised after his flippant and ill-considered comparison of Lord Ram and Lord Krishna. The controversy began during a recent Ram Katha in Karera in Madhya Pradesh's Shivpuri district. He said Ram stands straight, while Krishna stands bent at three places.

Article Title: 'Huge impact on polls': IB opposes shifting convict in ex-Punjab CM Beant Singh's assassination to state jail
Article Text:
Ex-Punjab CM murdered on August 31, 1995

Why is Hawara seeking a transfer?

NEW DELHI: The Intelligence Bureau (IB) on Tuesday opposed the transfer of Jagtar Singh Hawara, convicted in the 1995 assassination of then-Punjab chief minister Beant Singh, from Delhi's Tihar Jail to a prison in Punjab, telling the Supreme Court that the move could have a “huge impact” on the upcoming assembly elections in the state.The agency also classified Hawara as a high-risk prisoner and said he should not be shifted to Punjab. A bench of Justices M M Sundresh and P B Varale described the IB report as “very damning” while hearing Hawara's plea seeking a transfer to a prison in his home state.Senior advocate S Muralidhar, appearing for Hawara, told the court, “If elections are a concern, this may be taken up after three months.” The Supreme Court posted the matter for hearing in February next year. Elections to the 117-member Punjab Assembly are due early next year.Beant Singh, who served as Punjab chief minister from 1992 to 1995, was killed in a suicide bombing outside the state civil secretariat in Chandigarh on August 31, 1995. The blast also killed 16 others. Hawara, a member of the banned Babbar Khalsa International, was convicted in the assassination case and is serving a life sentence for the remainder of his natural life.Hawara's plea argues that he is a native of Punjab's Fatehgarh Sahib district and should be allowed to serve his sentence in a prison in the state. It also says there are no cases pending against him in Delhi and that his conduct in prison has been without blemish, apart from a jailbreak in January 2004.Hawara was among four inmates who escaped from Chandigarh's high-security Burail Jail on January 22, 2004, by digging a nearly 100-foot-long tunnel. The other escapees were Paramjit Singh Bheora, Jagtar Singh Tara and Devi Singh. Hawara and Bheora were subsequently arrested, while Tara was caught in Thailand. Devi Singh remains absconding.Opposing the transfer, Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati, appearing for the Delhi government, had earlier told the Supreme Court that Hawara's jailbreak history raised the risk of another escape. She also cited a Union home ministry advisory on the transfer of high-risk prisoners and the Punjab government's concerns over the possible impact on law and order.Hawara was sentenced to death by a trial court in March 2007. The Punjab and Haryana High Court commuted the sentence to life imprisonment in October 2010, directing that he should not be released for the rest of his life. Appeals against the high court verdict are pending before the Supreme Court.
Article Summary: Jagtar Singh Hawara was convicted in the 1995 assassination of then-Punjab chief minister Beant Singh. Hawara is serving a life sentence for the remainder of his natural life. He is seeking a transfer to a prison in his home state of Punjab. Elections to the 117-member Punjab Assembly are due early next year.

NEW DELHI: Bharatiya Janata Party ( BJP ) on Tuesday launched a scathing attack on Congress leader and leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi , accusing him of treason, promoting anarchy and attempting to undermine India's democratic institutions.BJP national spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia labelled Rahul Gandhi 'gaddar' (traitor) and 'Bhasmasur', alleging that his political approach was aimed at destabilising the country and weakening its constitutional framework.Addressing a press conference in New Delhi, Bhatia questioned Rahul Gandhi's foreign engagements, raised allegations over the Congress's memorandum of understanding (MoU) with the Communist Party of China (CCP) and demanded answers about the alleged funding of protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar."This issue is about the model of anarchy, disorder, and treason that the Leader of the Opposition is presenting to the country... That is why he is being referred to as 'Rahul Gaddar'," Bhatia said.He also accused Rahul of advocating unconstitutional regime change and attempting to weaken democratic institutions.Bhatia described Rahul Gandhi as a destructive force and accused him of promoting anarchy instead of respecting India's democratic framework."If India has one greatest strength, it lies in its democratic government, its reverence for the Constitution, and the stability it has maintained for 12 years. On the other hand, there is an opposition that is anarchic in its thinking, anti-Constitution, and openly speaks of overthrowing the government. Rahul Gandhi believes in anarchy and destruction; it is not for nothing that he is called a 'Bhasmasura' (a destructive force). He has become the kind of leader who seeks to usher in anarchy by killing democracy, strangling it to death," he said.The BJP spokesperson alleged that the opposition was seeking to overthrow elected governments and undermine constitutional institutions, including Parliament and the Supreme Court."The other ideology says that whatever you build, our only task is to destroy it. That is why Rahul Gandhi is not called Bhasmasur without reason. If anyone is attempting to destroy these institutions, it is Rahul Gandhi," he said.Bhatia also targeted Gandhi, former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee and former Bihar deputy chief minister Tejashwi Yadav over their alleged support for regime change.He warned that repeated calls for regime change could instead turn public opinion against the opposition and threaten the political future of its leaders."I say this with a lot of responsibility: people wanting a regime change might witness a situation where the people of the country feel that the Opposition is irresponsible and should be changed. The public will find an alternative to the opposition; do not imagine, Rahul Gandhi, Mamata Banerjee, or Tejashwi Yadav, that you will gain anything through anarchy. This public will put an end to your political careers. India’s democracy will remain unscathed," he said.The remarks came amid a controversy over the use of the phrase 'regime change' by senior advocate Prashant Bhushan, All India Students Association (AISA) president Neha Bora and Congress spokesperson Pawan Khera during public statements and press conferences in Delhi.The comments were made in the context of protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Bhatia also questioned Rahul Gandhi's meetings with foreign figures, including US Congresswoman Ilhan Omar and Mushfiqul Fazal, whom he accused of adopting anti-India positions."How can the leader of opposition in India be anti-India? How can he betray the nation?... The central question is why Rahul Gandhi is meeting individuals like Ilhan Omar or Mushfiqul Fazal who adopt anti-India stances. Is there any discussion about weakening India and bringing about regime change?" he asked.He further demanded that Gandhi disclose the contents of the Congress's MoU with the Communist Party of China and explain the alleged funding behind protests."Rahul Gandhi signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Communist Party of China (CCP) but has not disclosed what it contains to this day... He must also clarify where the funding for these protests, which are being organized with the aim of creating anarchy, is coming from."The BJP spokesperson also accused Gandhi of inappropriate physical conduct with a woman police officer during an anti-CEC protest on Ashoka Road near Jantar Mantar."Rahul Gandhi's inappropriate touching of a woman police officer is disgraceful. No political position gives anyone the right to touch a woman inappropriately. He must answer for his shameful behaviour," Bhatia said.He argued that Gandhi's position as Leader of the Opposition did not give him the right to behave inappropriately with security personnel.In his concluding remarks, Bhatia accused Rahul Gandhi and other opposition leaders of attempting to weaken India's democratic institutions and destabilise elected governments."Wherever there is an elected government, they want to overthrow it. They want to destroy constitutional institutions such as the Supreme Court and Parliament, as well as historical monuments," he said.The BJP leader maintained that India's democratic framework and constitutional institutions would remain strong despite what he described as the opposition's attempts to create disorder.
Article Summary: BJP national spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia labelled Rahul Gandhi 'gaddar' (traitor) and 'Bhasmasur', alleging that his political approach was aimed at destabilising the country. Article Title: India, Israel vote against Pakistan-backed UN arms control resolution: What it means
Article Text:
In a significant move, India and Israel opposed a UN resolution proposed by Pakistan and Belarus concerning regional arms control.

India and Israel have voted against a Pakistan- and Belarus-sponsored draft resolution at the united nations seeking conventional arms control at regional and subregional levels, with New Delhi arguing that national security concerns cannot be restricted by geographical boundaries.The draft resolution, titled ‘General and complete disarmament: Conventional arms control at the regional and subregional levels’, was adopted by the UN general assembly’s First Committee on Monday, receiving 180 votes in favour, two against and no abstentions.According to the news agency PTI, India and Israel were the only two countries among the 193 UN member states to oppose the resolution.Explaining India's position, Anmol Sher Bedi, first secretary at India's permanent mission to the UN, maintained that conventional arms control was a global issue and should not be addressed primarily through regional and subregional frameworks.“We are not fully convinced that it should be pursued primarily in regional and sub-regional contexts,” Bedi said while presenting India's explanation of vote before the UNGA first committee.He added that New Delhi's opposition was in line with its consistent position on the matter.India also raised questions over the resolution's call for the UN disarmament commission to develop principles that could provide a framework for regional agreements on conventional arms control.“We read this request with a certain degree of curiosity,” Bedi said, pointing out that the commission had already reached three consensus-based outcomes on related issues.These included guidelines and recommendations on regional disarmament adopted in 1993, guidelines on conventional arms control and disarmament finalised in 1999, and recommendations on practical confidence-building measures concerning conventional weapons agreed upon in 2017.“That makes three consensus outcomes on this very subject in the very body now being asked to start from scratch,” he said.Questioning the need for further discussions, Bedi said it was difficult to understand why an issue that had already undergone extensive deliberations needed to be taken up again, unless the intention was to keep the UN's disarmament machinery occupied.India also criticised the resolution's emphasis on maintaining a balance in defence capabilities within regional and subregional settings.Bedi argued that the approach wrongly presumed that countries' security interests were confined to their immediate geographical neighbourhoods.“This assumes that the security concerns of States politely stop at their regional borders. They do not,” he said.He further stressed that national security considerations often extend beyond narrowly defined regional boundaries, adding that the idea of maintaining a military balance within a particular region or subregion was unrealistic.The resolution argues that conventional arms control should primarily be pursued at regional and subregional levels, as most threats to international peace and security in the post-Cold War period have emerged among countries within the same geographical regions.It also calls for promoting agreements that strengthen regional peace and security while maintaining armaments and military forces at the lowest possible levels.Separately, India voted against a paragraph referring to conventional arms control proposals concerning South Asia.The paragraph took note of initiatives undertaken in various regions, including consultations among certain latin American countries and proposals for conventional arms control in South Asia, while acknowledging the importance of such measures for regional security.The resolution further states that militarily significant countries and nations possessing greater military capabilities have a special responsibility to advance agreements aimed at strengthening regional peace and security.
Article Summary: India and Israel voted against a Pakistan- and Belarus-sponsored draft resolution at the united nations seeking conventional arms control at regional and subregional levels. New Delhi argued that national security concerns cannot be restricted by geographical boundaries. The draft resolution was adopted by the UN general assembly’s First Committee on Monday.

Article Title: $445m down the drain? Elon Musk's Republican gamble fails; 'guess my election-interfering space lasers didn’t work'
Article Text:
Musk, who emerged as one of the biggest losers of election night, spent an estimated $445 million backing Republican candidates and causes. More than $200 million went towards Texas-related efforts alone.

Musk responds with 'space lasers' jibe

Democratic Congress could spell more trouble for Musk

Tech billionaire Elon Musk 's record-breaking $445 million bet on Republican candidates has failed to deliver the political victories he hoped for. Several of his preferred candidates suffered defeats in the US mid-term elections.From Texas to Ohio, the results dealt a major blow to Musk's political influence, while a surprise Democratic victory in Texas also raised questions over his ambitious plans to expand data centre operations in the state.Musk, who emerged as one of the biggest losers of election night, spent an estimated $445 million backing Republican candidates and causes. More than $200 million went towards Texas-related efforts alone. His spending made him the largest individual political donor in modern US history and set a record for money spent by a non-candidate during an election cycle. Yet, the candidates he supported were defeated across several key contests.The defeats included Ken Paxton's Senate race in Texas and Vivek Ramaswamy's bid for governor in Ohio. The biggest setback for Musk, however, could be in Texas, where Democrat Gina Hinojosa secured a surprise victory over incumbent Republican Greg Abbott in the gubernatorial race.The result has implications beyond Musk's political investments. Texas had emerged as a major destination for companies seeking to build data centres and expand artificial intelligence infrastructure. The state was seen as a favourable environment for such projects at a time when communities across the US were increasingly resisting large data centre developments over concerns about their impact.Musk's companies have significant ambitions in the state. Hinojosa's victory could now introduce uncertainty over the political and regulatory environment surrounding future data centre projects."Amid data center backlash all across the country, Texas was supposed to be an AI oasis, where people would be able to build data centers no matter what was happening in the rest of America," Politico reported quoting Sam Koppelman, the publisher of Hunterbrook Media, an investigative journalism outlet connected to a hedge fund, "This election totally changed that."As the Republican losses became clear, Musk turned to sarcasm on X early Wednesday. The billionaire, who had spent hundreds of millions of dollars backing candidates, appeared to poke fun at the election outcome and the criticism surrounding his political involvement."Guess my election-interfering space lasers didn't work this time 🤷‍♂️," Musk posted shortly before 1.15am ET.He followed it with another remark that appeared to reference the Democratic victory in Texas and the uncertainty surrounding his data centre plans."Data centers in space looking pretty appealing right now," he wrote.The posts came after an election in which Musk's financial backing failed to translate into victories for several of the Republican candidates he supported. His comments also brought attention to the potential business implications of the results, particularly in Texas.Musk could face another challenge as Democrats are expected to take control of both chambers of Congress, potentially with comfortable majorities. The shift in power could give them greater scope to scrutinise the influence of wealthy technology executives and their financial involvement in political campaigns.Musk has been a prominent Republican donor and an outspoken supporter of candidates aligned with the party. His record-breaking election spending could make him a particular focus for Democrats, who have argued that technology billionaires wield disproportionate influence over American politics.Representative Greg Casar, a Democrat from Texas, said voters had rejected Republican candidates partly because of their association with wealthy AI investors."Voters rejected Republicans in part because they were bought and paid for by AI billionaires," Casar said in a statement on Tuesday evening, as per a report by Politico."Democrats must hold them accountable instead of cashing their checks."The comments signal the possibility of a more confrontational relationship between Musk and a Democratic-controlled Congress. With Democrats expected to take over key leadership positions in both chambers, scrutiny of the political influence and spending of major technology executives could intensify.
Article Summary: Elon Musk's record-breaking $445 million bet on Republican candidates has failed to deliver the political victories he hoped for. Several of his preferred candidates suffered defeats in the US mid-term elections. Results dealt a major blow to Musk's political influence, while a surprise Democratic victory in Texas also raised questions over his ambitious plans to expand data centre operations in the state.

Article Title: Riyadh airport attack: Second Indian national succumbs to injuries, death toll reaches 14
Article Text:
Smoke and flames rise from King Khalid Airport, after Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis said they attacked the airport, in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia

The death toll from the October 10 attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh has risen to 14 after a second Indian national injured in the strike died in hospital, the Indian Embassy in Saudi Arabia said on Wednesday.The victim, whose identity has not been disclosed, had been critically injured and was being treated in an intensive care unit (ICU). The embassy said it had remained in contact with the family throughout the treatment and would help arrange the repatriation of the mortal remains to India or a funeral in Riyadh, as the family wishes.At least 11 Indian nationals were injured in the attack. In an update on October 23, the embassy said two were still in the ICU, two were in general hospital wards and seven had been discharged. The first Indian fatality was identified as Mohammed Yousuf Ali, whose funeral was held in Riyadh on October 12.Saudi Arabia's General Authority of Civil Aviation had initially reported 12 deaths and 309 injuries in the attack. The toll rose to 13 after the first injured Indian national died and has now reached 14.Saudi Arabia blamed Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels for the attack, although the group did not officially claim responsibility. The strike was part of a wider escalation in attacks on Saudi infrastructure amid the renewed conflict in Yemen.The latest death also comes amid a rising toll among Indians caught up in the wider West Asia conflict. A November 4 report by Hindustan Times put the number of Indians killed in the conflict since February at 24, including 15 seafarers.
Article Summary: The death toll from the October 10 attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh has risen to 14. At least 11 Indian nationals were injured in the attack. The first Indian fatality was identified as Mohammed Yousuf Ali, whose funeral was held in Riyadh on October 12. The latest death also comes amid a rising toll among Indians caught up in the wider West Asia conflict.

Article Title: Abdul El-Sayed wasn't supposed to be a politician. Now he's America's 1st Muslim senator
Article Text:
(Photo: Reuters) Democratic candidate for US Senate, Abdul El-Sayed, listens to his wife, Sarah Jukaku, during a campaign rally

Democratic US Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed speaks after his victory in the US midterm elections. (Reuters Photo)

'I believe life in America shouldn't be this hard'

Vocal critic of Israel

(Photo: AP) Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed speaks at an election night event, early Wednesday in Detroit, as his wife Sarah Jukaku watches.

From medical school to the US Senate

(Photo Reuters) Supporters celebrate outside the venue for the Election Night rally of Democratic US Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed during the US midterm elections in Detroit, Michigan

A second consecutive defeat

US Midterms 2026 In Numbers

The Karnataka connection

Democrat Abdul El-Sayed has defeated Republican Mike Rogers in the race for a US Senate seat in Michigan, marking a victory for the former public health official who entered politics after training as a doctor.With his victory, El-Sayed has made history as the first Muslim elected to the US Senate.The closely fought contest marks a breakthrough for the party’s progressive faction and prevents Republicans from flipping the seat being vacated by retiring Democratic Senator Gary Peters.El-Sayed campaigned on an agenda centred on universal healthcare and government accountability in one of the country's key political battleground states.The Michigan race had drawn national attention as Democrats sought to regain control of the Senate.Rogers, a former congressman and chairman of the House Intelligence Committee, was making a second attempt to win a Senate seat after losing to Democrat Elissa Slotkin by fewer than 20,000 votes in 2024.For El-Sayed, the victory marks the culmination of a political journey that began with a career in medicine. According to his campaign website, he initially trained to become a doctor but came to believe that failures in the political system were contributing to people's health problems.He has since built his career around public health and government administration, including serving as director of the Wayne County Department of Health, Human and Veterans Services.His campaign focused on the idea that healthcare should be accessible to everyone and that government should work for ordinary Americans rather than wealthy individuals and corporations."I ran for the US Senate because I believe life in America shouldn't be this hard," El-Sayed said on his campaign website, adding that he would fight to build a government that worked for people rather than "Elon Musk, Donald Trump, or their billionaire friends".His campaign website also described him as someone who "wasn't supposed to be a politician".The Michigan contest was marked by disagreements over US support for Israel and accusations of antisemitism.El-Sayed, who has been a vocal critic of Israel, faced criticism over his response to a March attack on a Michigan synagogue. He later apologised to those who felt his comments were hurtful.Republicans also sought to link him to controversial political streamer Hasan Piker, with whom he had appeared during the Democratic primary.President Donald Trump repeatedly referred to El-Sayed as a "jihadist", although Republicans produced no evidence linking him to terrorist organisations.Born and raised in southeast Michigan, El-Sayed attended public schools and captained his high school football, wrestling and lacrosse teams.He graduated from the University of Michigan with the highest distinction and played for its men's lacrosse team. He later earned a medical degree from Columbia University through a National Institutes of Health-funded fellowship and completed a second doctorate at the University of Oxford as a Rhodes Scholar.His father, Mohamed, is an Egyptian immigrant, while his stepmother, Jackie, belongs to a family that has lived in Michigan's Gratiot County since the 1800s.El-Sayed lives in Ann Arbor with Sarah and their two daughters, Emmalee and Serene.Rogers, 63, a former congressman and FBI agent, entered the contest with the backing of Trump and national Republicans. He sought to portray El-Sayed as a radical candidate sympathetic to Islamic extremism, citing alleged links to the Muslim Brotherhood, Reuters reported.The defeat marks Rogers' second consecutive loss in a Michigan Senate race. He narrowly lost the 2024 contest to Democrat Elissa Slotkin, even as Trump carried the state in that year's presidential election.El-Sayed's victory gives Democrats a win in a state that has not elected a Republican to the US Senate since 1994.El-Sayed's victory also has a personal connection to coastal Karnataka through his wife, Dr Sarah Jukaku, a psychiatrist whose family traces its roots to Bhatkal, around 140km from Mangaluru.Sarah is the granddaughter of Jukaku Shamshuddin, who served as deputy minister for finance in Mysore State under then chief minister BD Jatti.A Rhodes Scholar, El-Sayed met Sarah while they were students at the University of Michigan. He has spoken about his connection with her South Indian family and culture."Listen, I've been married in a South Indian family for 20 years, like. I'm well inducted now. You know, I might be more Indian than I'm Arab," he said in an interview.While the family has its roots in Bhatkal, most of its members are now settled in Bengaluru. Sarah's immediate family, meanwhile, has largely remained in the US.
Article Summary: Abdul El-Sayed has defeated Republican Mike Rogers in the race for a US Senate seat in Michigan. The former public health official entered politics after training as a doctor. He campaigned on an agenda centred on universal healthcare and government accountability in one of the country's key political battleground states.

Article Title: US election results: Amy Acton defeats Donald Trump-backed Vivek Ramaswamy to become Ohio's first woman governor
Article Text:
Democrat Amy Acton wins Ohio governor’s race, ending 20-year Republican hold

Acton capitalises on affordability concerns and Ramaswamy's wealth

Attack ad featuring Acton's estranged mother sparks backlash

Former pandemic health director returns to state leadership

Poll Vote & Share your view What aspect of Acton's campaign resonated most with voters? Focus on affordable healthcare Making daily expenses more affordable Her personal life story Support for working- and middle-class families 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Democrat Dr Amy Acton has won the race for governor of Ohio, defeating Trump-backed Indian-American Republican candidate, Vivek Ramaswamy , to become the first woman elected to the state's top office.Her victory also marks the first time in 20 years that a Democrat has won the governorship.Acton, a public health physician and former Ohio health director during the Covid-19 pandemic, overcame more than $100 million spent against her by Ramaswamy and his Republican allies.She will succeed Republican Governor Mike DeWine, who is barred from seeking another term.The 60-year-old built her campaign around affordability and improved access to healthcare, appealing to working- and middle-class voters by highlighting her personal background. An Ohio native, Acton has spoken about spending part of her childhood homeless and living in a tent for one winter.Her victory comes as Democrats seek to regain ground in Ohio, where voters have increasingly shifted towards Republicans during Donald Trump's political rise.Acton's campaign sought to portray Ramaswamy, a biotech billionaire and former 2024 presidential candidate, as out of touch with ordinary voters facing higher living costs.The campaign highlighted concerns over the cost of living, fuel prices and the impact of Trump's tariffs. Ramaswamy and his Republican allies spent more than $100 million during the contest.Billionaire Elon Musk also contributed at least $5 million to a political action committee aligned with the Republican candidate, according to the AP.Acton won despite repeated campaign appearances by Trump and Vice President JD Vance, an Ohio native, who travelled to the state in the final weeks to rally support for Ramaswamy and Republican Senator Jon Husted.Ramaswamy had secured early backing from Ohio Republicans, with DeWine appointing Husted, then the leading Republican contender for governor, to the US Senate after Vance vacated the seat to become vice-president.The decision to endorse Ramaswamy, a newcomer to Ohio politics, forced several established Republican politicians, including the state attorney general and treasurer, to reconsider their political plans.Ramaswamy also faced resistance during the Republican primary from Casey “The Car Guy” Putsch, a vehicle designer and YouTube personality whose campaign attracted nearly 18 per cent of the Republican vote despite spending only $130,000. Putsch later announced that he planned to vote for Acton.The campaign was also marked by controversy over an advertisement aired by Ramaswamy in its final month. The 60-second spot featured Acton's estranged mother, Donna Arthur, accusing her daughter of lying about her upbringing and urging voters not to support her.Arthur called Acton “a liar” with a “serious problem” with being honest about her past. The advertisement drew criticism after details emerged about the family's history. Arthur had been estranged from Acton for nearly 50 years and had lost custody of her children after her husband, their stepfather, was indicted for raping Acton when she was a child.The man pleaded not guilty and fled the state before he could stand trial, the AP reported.The advertisement initially surfaced online before Ramaswamy claimed responsibility for it. He defended the campaign as a criticism of what he described as a pattern of deception by Acton, disputing claims that it questioned whether she had been abused as a child.Trump and Vance defended Ramaswamy's decision to use the advertisement. Trump also expressed jealousy that he had never had the opportunity to run a similar attack against a political rival.However, the advertisement triggered bipartisan criticism, including from five former Ohio governors, senior politicians from both parties, women's groups and several hundred alumni of Ramaswamy's Catholic high school in Cincinnati. Critics described it as gutter politics and called on him to withdraw it.The campaign eventually took the advertisement off the air about a week before Election Day, after spending roughly a quarter of the $4 million advertising budget it had announced.Acton became one of Ohio Democrats' most recognisable figures during the early months of the Covid-19 pandemic, when she appeared in statewide broadcasts alongside DeWine and Husted.During the campaign, Ramaswamy and his allies criticised her role in the state's pandemic response, arguing that she had been too aggressive in shutting down schools and businesses. DeWine defended his former health director, saying responsibility for the decisions ultimately rested with him, although he continued to endorse Ramaswamy.Acton enters the governor's office without having previously held elected office. Her predecessor, DeWine, is 79 and is expected to retire from electoral politics after five decades in public life.
Article Summary: Amy Acton, a public health physician and former Ohio health director during the Covid-19 pandemic, overcame more than $100 million spent against her by Vivek Ramaswamy and his Republican allies. She will succeed Republican Governor Mike DeWine, who is barred from seeking another term.

Article Title: Princess Catherine’s sister Pippa Middleton and husband James Matthews ordered to demolish unauthorised car park at £15.5 million estate; neighbours raise concerns over construction without consultati
Article Text:
Pippa Middleton and James Matthews have faced criticism from locals over construction and public access to their estate. (Photo: Instagram/Google Maps)

Council rules car park development was visually intrusive

Neighbours objected to construction without consultation

Pippa Middleton and husband James Matthews have been ordered to demolish an unauthorised car park at their £15.5 million estate. (Photo: Instagram)

Pippa Middleton and James Matthews' previous dispute with locals

Pippa Middleton and her hedge fund manager husband, James Matthews, have been ordered to remove a car park they built on their sprawling country estate without obtaining prior planning permission. The decision comes after a group of residents in the picturesque village of Kintbury raised objections with West Berkshire Council, claiming they had not been consulted before construction began last year.Pippa, the younger sister of Princess Catherine, and James own the land, which forms part of their £15.5 million, 145-acre Barton Court estate. The couple moved into the property in 2022 and have since been involved in several disagreements with locals over developments and access to the estate.According to a report by The Times, the couple subsequently applied for retrospective planning permission for the anglers' car park, arguing that the sale of fishing rights along the River Kennet was a significant source of income that helped support the upkeep of the estate.However, West Berkshire Council rejected the proposal, concluding that the development was 'visually intrusive and urbanised' and had 'eroded a measure of the open and undeveloped rural character' of the North Wessex Downs.The couple have now been directed to remove the car park.The development reportedly involved laying approximately 400 square metres of agricultural hard standing across a meadow. The land was previously known among residents as the grazing ground of two heavy horses, Monty and Drummer, who lived there before the estate changed hands.The car park drew considerable criticism from residents, who approached the council after noticing the construction. In objections submitted to the authorities, locals said they were 'shocked' by the development and questioned why the community had not been consulted before work began.Some residents also alleged that the car park had been created to move vehicles away from areas closer to the couple's home, thereby preserving the views around their property.One objector reportedly wrote: 'This application is to move unsightly parking out of sight of the applicants on entry to the Barton Court estate to the detriment of the residents and the heritage of Kintbury.'Another resident highlighted concerns about the location, traffic congestion and the potential impact on the area's heritage, requesting that the planning committee conduct a site inspection before reaching a decision.Planners also raised concerns about the absence of mitigation measures to protect the River Kennet from potential adverse environmental impacts.This is not the first time Pippa and James have faced opposition from local residents since moving to Barton Court. The couple had earlier drawn criticism for restricting public access to Mill Lane, a route running through their estate that had reportedly been used by dog walkers and ramblers for years.The Grade I-listed Barton Court, located along the River Kennet near Kintbury, was previously owned by the late retail tycoon Sir Terence Conran, who had permitted members of the public to use the lane.However, after Pippa and James moved into the property with their three children, Arthur, Grace and Rose, in 2022, an electric gate was installed to restrict public access. Signs stating ‘Private: No Public Access’ and ‘No Trespassing’ also appeared across the estate.The move prompted 35 residents, backed by the Ramblers Association, to approach West Berkshire Council, seeking official recognition of Mill Lane as a public right of way.An inquiry by the Planning Inspectorate into the dispute began at the village hall in May. James Matthews also attended the proceedings, where he reportedly argued that the family's security and privacy concerns should be considered.
Article Summary: Council rules car park development was visually intrusive and urbanised. Neighbours objected to construction without consultation by West Berkshire Council. Couple moved into the property in 2022 and have since been involved in several disagreements with locals over developments and access to the estate.

Article Title: Entire full-time police force resigns in Georgia city; Mayor Craig Timmons admits placing GPS tracker on Milner Police Chief's truck over timesheet concerns; Lamar Bunn denies wrongdoing
Article Text:
Mayor Craig Timmons admitted placing a GPS tracking device on Milner Police Chief Lamar Bunn's truck. (Photo: Channel 2 Action News)

Why did the Georgia mayor track the police chief's vehicle?

Police Chief Lamar Bunn denied wrongdoing amid the controversy over the tracking device and his working hours. (Photo: Channel 2 Action News)

Police chief Lamar Bunn denies wrongdoing

Entire full-time police department resigns

The entire full-time police force in Milner, Georgia, resigned, triggering a law enforcement crisis in the small city. (Photo: ​Channel 2 Action News)

Sheriff’s office to provide police coverage

Mayor says he wants to do what is right

A small city in Georgia is facing a police staffing crisis after its entire full-time police force resigned, with Mayor Craig Timmons confirming that he placed a GPS tracking device on the police chief's vehicle amid concerns over the officer's working hours.In an interview with WSB-TV's Channel 2 Action News, Timmons admitted that he had installed a tracking device on the truck driven by Milner Police Chief Lamar Bunn. He also confirmed placing a surveillance camera near a car wash, pointing towards City Hall, where the police chief's office is located.The mayor said his concerns were related to Bunn's timesheets, which required his signature. Timmons said he wanted to establish whether the chief was accurately accounting for his working hours.The admission comes after the chief, all five full-time police officers and most reserve personnel resigned, with their departures taking effect on October 28, 2026. The mass resignation has raised questions about the leadership of the department and how the city will maintain law enforcement services.Speaking to Channel 2 Action News, Timmons was directly asked whether he had placed a tracking device on the police vehicle used by Bunn."Yes, sir. I did," the mayor confirmed.He was also asked about a video camera installed near a car wash and pointed towards the building where the police chief's office is located. Timmons acknowledged that as well, saying it had been done with the property owner's approval.Explaining his decision, the mayor said he was required to sign off on the police chief's timesheets but had concerns about the hours being reported. He further revealed that he had prepared a report outlining allegations related to Bunn's timekeeping and use of city vehicles, which he planned to present at a special city council meeting.Timmons defended his actions, maintaining that his role as mayor included overseeing the city's administrative functioning and ensuring accountability..Bunn, however, has denied any wrongdoing. Speaking to the news channel by phone, he explained that his responsibilities as police chief were not restricted to working inside the police station or within the city's limits.He said he regularly handled administrative duties remotely, including responding to emails and monitoring police radio communications. He also maintained that his work continued beyond regular office hours."My job doesn't stop when I leave the office," Bunn said, explaining that he had even continued working while on vacation in Panama City.Assistant Chief Chris Landers also defended the department's working arrangements, saying it was common for officers to work outside the city and receive calls after regular working hours.Bunn's position was that his work responsibilities extended beyond a fixed workplace and schedule.The controversy has unfolded against the backdrop of an unprecedented staffing crisis for Milner. The chief and all five full-time officers submitted their resignations, with the departures taking effect on October 28. Most reserve personnel also reportedly left the department.A resignation letter obtained by WSB-TV cited concerns about the "judgment and decision-making" of the mayor and certain city council members regarding the police department.The tracking device was among the issues that reportedly contributed to the officers' concerns.
