An officer who spoke to the news channel also pointed to restrictions on opportunities to take up off-duty jobs as a possible factor.Timmons, however, said there had been a miscommunication over the issue and maintained that neither he nor the city council had issued an order restricting officers from taking such work.Bunn also said he had not asked the officers to resign.With Milner's full-time police department no longer operational, Lamar County Sheriff Brad White said his deputies would continue responding to calls in the city, as they had previously done.He indicated that if the absence of a local police department continued for an extended period, Milner would need to enter into a formal arrangement with the sheriff's office for police services.Timmons said he remained confident that the city would be able to rebuild its police department. He also claimed that he had already started receiving unsolicited applications from people interested in police positions, as well as the city manager's role.City Manager Tausha Grose also resigned shortly after the police department's mass departure, according to local reports.During the interview, Timmons defended his actions and spoke about his personal journey, including his recovery from drug addiction and his religious faith."Right is right and wrong is wrong," he said, adding that he had turned his life over to Jesus 15 years ago and had made a promise to do right by the people he encountered.The situation has left the small Georgia city dealing with more than a dispute over a police chief's timesheets. With its full-time officers gone, Milner now faces the challenge of restoring its police department while addressing the concerns about leadership and trust that surfaced in the resignation letters.
Article Summary: Mayor Craig Timmons admitted to placing a GPS tracking device on police chief Lamar Bunn's truck. He also confirmed placing a surveillance camera near a car wash, pointing towards City Hall, where the police chief's office is located. Timmons said he wanted to establish whether the chief was accurately accounting for his working hours. The admission comes after the chief, all five full-time police officers and most reserve personnel resigned, with their departures taking effect on October 28.

Article Title: Why America’s AI data center companies are turning to airplane ‘graveyards’
Article Text:
Representative image

Tapping massive ‘power reserves’

At a time when the artificial intelligence (AI) boom has sparked a surge in electricity demand, American AI data centre companies are finding new ways to power their infrastructure. While some are turning towards massive solar and wind farms, others are striking deals to use nuclear power to keep the servers running. Now, they are reportedly turning to Arizona’s Sonoran desert where thousands of retired airplanes with jet engines mounted sit in vast metal graveyards. Those turbines are being resurrected to keep the servers running. The New York Times reported that a growing roster of engineering firms is stripping engines from decommissioned aircraft and converting them into stationary electrical generators with data center operators snapping them up as fast as they can be built.“They’re getting creative. Just a few years ago, a traditional data center would have been like, ‘Are you kidding me? This is ridiculous’,” said Bill Kleyman, chief executive of AI platform and infrastructure provider Apolo. Today, attitudes have fundamentally shifted around project lead times. Data center developers are now singularly obsessed with "speed to power," Kleyman explained, adding, “It’s like, ‘How fast can you get me energy?’”The rush to secure self-contained energy sources has also been accelerated by political pressure.With rapid data centre construction driving public backlash over rising household utility bills, President Donald Trump has pushed facilities to generate their own power rather than pulling from local grids.“It was my idea. Data centers now are mandated by me that they build their own electricity, so they’re not taking it from the grid,” Trump told reporters in August.Aircraft graveyards offer an enormous, untapped energy reserve, the report pointed out. In January, the federal Energy Information Administration estimated that the engines housed inside 4,000 retired military jets parked at a single desert base in Tucson could produce 40,000 megawatts of electricity, exceeding the generation capacity of the entire state of Arizona.Converted aircraft turbines, however, come with major engineering trade-offs. For example, repurposed jet engines are generally less fuel-efficient than turbines built specifically for modern gas-fired power plants. Moreover, because of their lower operational efficiency, data centers require a higher number of jet-powered units to produce the equivalent electrical output. Converted engines release significantly higher volumes of air pollutants into surrounding communities.Elon Musk’s AI venture, xAI, has already integrated eight converted jet turbines to power a major data center in Mississippi, according to state regulatory filings and satellite imagery reviewed by The New York Times. State permits granted to the facility allow the converted turbines to emit carbon monoxide at double the rate permitted for other on-site turbines, along with a 25% higher ceiling for volatile organic compounds (VOCs). Both substances present serious health hazards.Environmental organisations and community advocates argue that leaning on older, dirtier turbines undermines clean energy goals. The Southern Environmental Law Center has formally challenged Mississippi’s regulatory approval of xAI’s turbines, arguing that the equipment maker has failed to supply documentation proving compliance with standards for toxins like formaldehyde, while accusing xAI of undercounting its projected emissions.
Article Summary: AI data centre companies are finding new ways to power their infrastructure. Some are turning towards massive solar and wind farms, others are striking deals to use nuclear power. Now, they are reportedly turning to Arizona’s Sonoran desert where thousands of retired airplanes with jet engines mounted sit in vast metal graveyards.

Article Title: ‘Habibi, call me Senator’: First Muslim US Senator Abdul El-Sayed mocks Donald Trump, JD Vance in victory speech
Article Text:
Abdul El-Sayed trolls Trump, JD Vance after winning Michigan Senate race

El-Sayed's campaign and attacks from Trump

Democratic gains reshape Senate politics

Democrat candidate Abdul El-Sayed on Wednesday took a swipe at US President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance after defeating Republican Mike Rogers in Michigan's Senate race, using his victory speech to highlight the irony of Vance having to formally swear him into office.Addressing Vance, El-Sayed said, “Habibi, there is this delicious irony in the fact that you’re constitutionally obligated to swear me in, in January.”He also directed a pointed message at Trump, who had repeatedly criticised him during the campaign and questioned his loyalty to the United States.“I know you struggle with my name, so after JD swears me in, you can just go on and call me Senator,” El-Sayed said.El-Sayed's victory makes him the first Muslim elected to the US Senate. He defeated Rogers, a former congressman and FBI agent who had Trump's backing, in a closely watched contest for Michigan's open Senate seat.El-Sayed also took aim at Rogers during his victory speech, telling supporters, “You chose hate, and Michigan chose hope.”The son of Egyptian immigrants, El-Sayed is a former public health official who had never held elected office before winning the Senate race. His victory followed a difficult political journey, eight years after he suffered a double-digit defeat in Michigan's Democratic gubernatorial primary.His campaign was built around a progressive platform that included universal healthcare, removing outside money from elections and criticism of Israel. He received support from progressive leaders, including Senator Bernie Sanders and Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez.The campaign was marked by repeated attacks from Trump and other Republicans, who sought to link El-Sayed to terrorist organisations despite no evidence of such ties. They also questioned his loyalty to the US.El-Sayed's criticism of Israel became a major point of contention, including during a bruising Democratic primary against Representative Haley Stevens. The primary drew nearly $60 million in outside spending, with the American Israel Public Affairs Committee (AIPAC) spending nearly $30 million opposing him, its largest investment in a single race.Stevens, who lost the primary, endorsed Rogers on November 1, saying El-Sayed had not done enough to address her and the Jewish community's concerns.El-Sayed also faced criticism over remarks following an attack on a Michigan synagogue earlier this year. He later apologised, saying he was “sorry” to “anyone who feels like my comments might have been hurtful”.El-Sayed's win came as Democrats secured control of both chambers of Congress in the midterm elections, according to Reuters. His victory was among several gains for the party in states that have traditionally favoured Republicans.The Michigan contest became a major focus in the battle for Senate control after two-term Democratic Senator Gary Peters decided not to seek re-election.Republicans had cleared the field for Rogers, who narrowly lost a Senate race to then-Representative Elissa Slotkin in 2024.However, his campaign faced challenges over his support for Trump as voters expressed concerns about rising prices linked to the war with Iran and the economic impact of the president's tariffs.Rogers, who had previously criticised Trump, had aligned himself more closely with the president in recent years.He had also voiced concern about the war with Iran, writing on social media in September, “The war with Iran needs to end, and end quickly.”El-Sayed's victory is expected to strengthen the progressive wing of the Democratic Party ahead of the 2028 presidential election.His campaign demonstrated the electoral reach of a platform centred on policies such as Medicare for All, which would replace the existing mix of private and public health insurance with a government-run, single-payer system.
Article Summary: Abdul El-Sayed is the first Muslim elected to the US Senate. He defeated Republican Mike Rogers in a closely watched contest for Michigan's open Senate seat. His victory is expected to strengthen the progressive wing of the Democratic Party ahead of the 2028 presidential election.

Article Title: Delhi govt counsel gives consent for criminal contempt proceedings against CJP leader Ratna Singh over ‘serving the master’ posts targeting Saket judge
Article Text:
Delhi government's Additional Standing Counsel has approved steps to initiate criminal contempt proceedings against Ratna Singh

Ratna Singh's posts against Saket court judge under scrutiny

Delhi counsel distinguishes judicial criticism from criminal contempt

CJP leaders' posts on Delhi Police, Special Executive Magistrate system

Delhi High Court to independently consider criminal contempt matter





NEW DELHI: The Delhi government's Additional Standing Counsel (Criminal) has given consent to initiate criminal contempt proceedings against Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leader Ratna Singh over her social media posts allegedly accusing a judicial officer of acting on the instructions of an unidentified "master".The counsel said the allegations prima facie raised concerns about the independence and impartiality of the judicial process and provided sufficient grounds to invoke the criminal contempt jurisdiction of the Delhi High Court Additional Standing Counsel Amol Sinha gave the consent in an opinion dated November 2, following representations by advocate Kausik Chatterjee seeking action against Singh over statements posted on social media platform X and remarks reported by the PTI.The controversy relates to proceedings before Chief Judicial Magistrate Abhinav Pandey at Saket Courts concerning Singh's alleged detention by the Delhi Police.In an order dated October 10, the magistrate had declined the relief sought by Singh in connection with the alleged detention.According to the representation examined by the government counsel, Singh subsequently posted messages on X expressing dissatisfaction with the judicial proceedings and making allegations about the conduct of the judicial officer.One of the posts allegedly said the "Judge" was "serving the master", while another suggested that both the Delhi Police and the judge were "following order from master".The representation argued that the statements went beyond criticism of a judicial order and questioned the independence and impartiality of the presiding officer.In his opinion, Sinha distinguished between criticism of a judicial decision, which is permissible, and allegations that a judicial officer acted under external influence or with improper motives."Judicial orders are open to criticism," the opinion noted, adding that an aggrieved person can challenge the reasoning, legality or correctness of an order through remedies available under the law.However, the opinion said the alleged statements that the judicial officer was "serving the master" or "following order from master" were not limited to questioning the merits of the order.It observed that such expressions prima facie suggested that the judicial officer was acting on instructions from an external authority rather than independently exercising judicial discretion in accordance with the law.Sinha further observed that publicly accusing an identifiable judicial officer of acting at the instance of an external authority, without providing any supporting factual basis, could create an impression that judicial decisions were being influenced by considerations beyond the merits of a case.According to the opinion, such allegations were prima facie capable of lowering the authority of the court and eroding public confidence in the administration of justice.The supplementary representation also referred to subsequent social media publications concerning preventive proceedings involving CJP leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka.These included statements about the functioning of the Special Executive Magistrate system.However, Sinha distinguished these publications from the specific allegations concerning the Chief Judicial Magistrate. He observed that the later posts were primarily directed at the conduct of the Delhi Police and the functioning of the Special Executive Magistrate system.He said that such statements could not be treated as criminal contempt merely because they contained strong criticism.Sinha accordingly accorded consent for taking appropriate steps to initiate criminal contempt proceedings against Singh under the procedure prescribed by Section 15(2) of the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971.The proceedings would be initiated through a motion moved by the competent law officer.The opinion clarified that its observations were based only on a prima facie assessment of the allegations and did not amount to a final finding of criminal contempt. The matter will remain subject to the independent consideration of the Delhi High Court.(With ANI inputs)
Article Summary: The controversy relates to proceedings before Chief Judicial Magistrate Abhinav Pandey at Saket Courts concerning Singh's alleged detention by the Delhi Police. Delhi government's Additional Standing Counsel (Criminal) has given consent to initiate criminal contempt proceedings against Singh.

Article Title: Friend, 2 aides strangle Delhi property dealer over suspected affair, stuff body in bag
Article Text:
The victim, Vinod, was a resident of Chhawla. (AI Image)





NEW DELHI: A 30-year-old property dealer was strangled, allegedly by three men, over suspicions of an illicit relationship in southwest Delhi's Dabri area last week. According to police, the suspects stuffed his body inside a bag, tied his hands with ropes, locked the flat and fled. Two of them have been arrested.The victim, Vinod, was a resident of Chhawla. According to preliminary investigation, he was invited for dinner to Bengali Colony, Mahavir Enclave, by his friend Yogesh alias Tinku on Oct 31 evening. Police said after dinner, Yogesh, along with his brother-in-law Munchun and their friend Chandan, allegedly strangled Vinod, put his body in a bag and left.Dabri police received information about the incident around 12.30pm Monday, following which the SHO, along with other cops, reached the spot and discovered Vinod's body.Police subsequently apprehended Yogesh alias Tinku (28) and Munchun (25). Munchun has been previously involved in theft and burglary cases, according to police. While Yogesh is educated up to Class XII, Munchun has studied up to Class VII. Chandan is absconding.According to investigators, Yogesh suspected Vinod of having an illicit relationship with his wife Shobha, who works in event management. During interrogation, he claimed Vinod had been speaking about his wife in derogatory terms.Yogesh also told cops that Vinod had loaned him some money to buy an air-conditioner and was now demanding it back. Police are verifying these claims.While police suspect an argument may have escalated into a physical scuffle on the day of the murder, they are also examining the evidence to ascertain if the crime was a premeditated one. "We are probing if the murder was being planned for weeks," a police source said.Meanwhile, the crime team and forensic science laboratory experts have inspected the crime scene and collected evidence, and the body has been sent for a post-mortem. A case under BNS Section 103(1) (murder) has been registered at Dabri police station. Further investigation is underway to establish the ascertain the sequence of events and the role of those allegedly involved.
Article Summary: Vinod, 30, was invited for dinner to Bengali Colony, Mahavir Enclave, by his friend Yogesh alias Tinku. Yogesh, along with his brother-in-law Munchun and their friend Chandan, allegedly strangled Vinod, put his body in a bag and left. Chandan is absconding.

Article Title: Delhi ACP suspended after police HQ demonstration over transfers
Article Text:
Assistant Commissioner Manasvi Vashistha was suspended for protesting his transfer along with Inspector Arun Kumar.

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you think police officers should have a formal platform to raise workplace grievances? Yes, to ensure their concerns are addressed No, existing grievance mechanisms are sufficient It depends on the nature of the issue 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





NEW DELHI: Hours after leading a protest outside and inside the police headquarters, assistant commissioner of police Manasvi Vashistha was suspended by the ministry of home affairs (MHA).The MHA order, dated Nov 2, said: “... The competent authority, in exercise of the powers conferred under Rule 10 of the CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965, hereby places Manasvi Vashistha, DANIPS (2019), under suspension with immediate effect.”It further ordered that during the suspension period, Vashistha’s headquarters shall be Delhi and he shall not leave Delhi without permission from the competent authority. During the suspension period, Vashistha would be entitled to a subsistence allowance equivalent to the leave salary he would have drawn, had he been on leave on half-average pay or half pay, along with dearness allowance, if admissible on the basis of such leave salary.Police sources said Vashistha has received his suspension letter.The development comes a day after hundreds of Delhi Police personnel gathered at the police headquarters to protest Vashistha and inspector Arun Kumar ’s transfers after a confrontation between police personnel and lawyers at Shahdara police station on Oct 23.Delhi Police, however, described the gathering as a ‘sampark sabha’ (interaction).The transfers followed an alleged scuffle in which an advocate suffered a serious head injury.Lawyers accused the two officers of misbehaviour and alleged that the ACP had brandished his pistol.Vashistha, previously posted in Gandhi Nagar, was transferred to the Special Police Unit for Women and Children (SPUWAC), while Shahdara SHO Kumar was moved to the security unit.Vashistha, whose transfer triggered the demonstration, led the protest. However, while speaking to reporters, he had said the mobilisation was an organic call by police personnel and that he had joined it. He said an application had been submitted seeking a platform to present their grievances before senior officers.Addressing the gathering, the ACP called for a clear standard operating procedure (SOP) to deal with lawyers entering police stations.He said the entry of more than five people wearing black coats should be treated as an unlawful assembly. He also demanded a cell at the police headquarters to address such incidents, immediate cancellation of bar licences in cases of misbehaviour with police personnel and the deployment of two companies of security forces at every court complex.
Article Summary: Manasvi Vashistha was suspended by the ministry of home affairs. He led a protest outside and inside the police headquarters. The development comes a day after hundreds of Delhi Police personnel gathered at the police HQ to protest his transfer. It followed an alleged scuffle in which an advocate suffered a serious head injury.

Article Title: Raj Thackeray calls off annual Dipotsav at Mumbai's Shivaji Park over severe drought in Maharashtra
Article Text:
MNS chief Raj Thackeray announced the cancellation of the annual Dipotsav celebration at Shivaji Park





MUMBAI: Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) chief Raj Thackeray on Wednesday said his party will not hold its annual Diwali celebration, Dipotsav, at Shivaji Park in Mumbai this year due to the severe drought in the state.In a video message, Thackeray also appealed to people in Maharashtra to celebrate Diwali mindfully, news agency PTI reported.He said it would not be prudent to celebrate festivals extravagantly when rural Maharashtra is reeling under a severe drought, farmers are facing financial pressure and thousands are migrating to cities as a result.The Maharashtra government has declared 85% of the state drought-hit following deficient rainfall this year and announced interim aid of Rs 5,000 to farmers before Diwali.Thackeray said the Dipotsav would be organised next year if the situation hopefully improves.The MNS' Dipotsav attracts thousands of people every year.Shivaji Park and the surrounding area are decorated with lights, while a synchronised firecracker display is part of the celebration, PTI reported.The event is inaugurated by prominent public figures. In 2023, then chief minister Eknath Shinde and deputy chief minister Devendra Fadnavis, who is now the chief minister, attended the celebrations. In 2024, legendary scriptwriters Salim Khan and Javed Akhtar inaugurated the Dipotsav.Last year, ahead of the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation polls, Raj Thackeray and his cousin, Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray, inaugurated the event together.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: MNS chief Raj Thackeray announced the cancellation of the annual Dipotsav celebration at Shivaji Park in Mumbai. He said it would not be prudent to celebrate festivals extravagantly when rural Maharashtra is reeling under a severe drought. The Maharashtra government has declared 85% of the state drought-hit following deficient rainfall.

Article Title: After Mumbai's Bandra’s Neville D’Souza ground, Girgaum volleyball ground faces threat from infrastructure project
Article Text:
A volleyball ground in Girgaum Chowpatty faces potential loss due to plans for an electrical sub-station (Representative image)

BJP min: 2 other sites available for tunnel infra





MUMBAI: Even as a sword hangs over the fate of Bandra’s Neville D’Souza football ground, a volleyball ground in Girgaum Chowpatty is facing an existential threat.An electrical sub-station for Orange Gate-Marine Drive underground road tunnel project has been planned on the ground, where, BJP minister Mangal Prabhat Lodha says, 300-500 people play every day.Stressing that infrastructure development should not come at the cost of public open spaces, he urged the district administration to preserve the ground at Mafatlal Gymkhana.He said there are at least two alternative sites available for the sub-station, a railway plot across the road and a site in Chowpatty where work had previously started for an underground sub-station.Lodha, along with several locals, met Mumbai city additional collector Bappasaheb Thorat and resident officer Shivananda Langdapure and asked the district administration to preserve the playground. He said there are at least two alternative sites available.A high-power committee had proposed setting up the substation on the volleyball ground. Lodha said nearly all members of the committee had agreed to consider the alternative sites.“Volleyball is a sport played by ordinary citizens. Every day, between 300 and 500 people play here from 6am onwards. Since alternatives are available, our request is that this ground be preserved for public use,” he said.Lodha said he had held discussions with MMRDA officials and senior members of the committee on the issue. A joint meeting will be convened after Diwali to arrive at a final solution, he said.
Article Summary: An electrical sub-station for Orange Gate-Marine Drive underground road tunnel project has been planned on the ground. BJP minister Mangal Prabhat Lodha says, 300-500 people play every day. He urged the district administration to preserve the ground at Mafatlal Gymkhana.

Article Title: 'Aren't we secular?' HC asks BMC to restore actor Dia Mirza's anti-cracker post
Article Text:
Actor Dia Mi­r­za





MUMBAI: Bombay HC said it's "unfortunate" BMC had removed from its social media pages a video of actor Dia Mirza urging citizens to avoid crackers as part of the anti-pollution drive. It suggested the post be "put back" to restore people's confidence, reports Rosy Sequeira.HC said it was "disturbed by comments in regard to celebrities who had participated and assisted in public cause". It further said, "There could not have been any other colour which could be given, and more particularly, when there are court directions." It asked, "How do you object to a person's participation? Are we not a secular country?"Celebrities were roped in for BMC’s campaign against firecrackers after HC’s nudge last week. Pointing out that it was “really upset” over actor Dia Mirza’s post being removed, Justices Girish Kulkarni and Neela Gokhale said, “We would desire that in the event any goodwill message of any celebrity was taken off from the corporation’s social media, it would be ideal if the same is put back in the spirit of what Supreme Court observed that the festival is for everybody to celebrate. ”Justice Kulkarni said they didn’t approve of BMC’s move. “Somebody is voluntarily coming forward, who has always been associated with social causes, and you are going to reprimand that person.With all this petty-mindedness.”The judges said Mirza “had rendered a very very good message in terms of environment, noise pollution and air pollution”. “There was nothing. There was no question of objection. No question of giving any colour. Most unfortunate,” said Justice Kulkarni.HC suggested that BMC reupload the video. “...it should not have been taken off... please put it again and restore the confidence of the people in the Constitution and society... This is a constitutional requirement, not this kind of thought. And these are stray thoughts of one or two persons,” said Justice KulkarniHC said environment, air and noise pollution are of paramount concerns, and every person can canvass and “bring this sensitisation to the public fore”. “Therefore, [asking] why X person was picked up etc is not a good thing,” said Justice Kulkarni.Hearing a suo motu PIL on festival noise and air pollution due to firecrackers, HC had on Oct 26 said it expected celebrities to voluntarily come forward to spread awareness. On Tuesday, the judges told BMC’s advocate Joel Carlos to congratulate civic chief Ashwini Bhide for the “impeccable steps she has taken”, particularly by getting celebrities to spread awareness. State’s advocate Jyoti Chavan said the HC order had created so much goodwill that celebrities “suo motu approached us”.The bench cited Supreme Court’s Monday order that Diwali is a national festival and also referred to raising of awareness by celebrities. It asked whether SC and HC orders have any qualification.The judges said their order seeking measures to keep the bursting of firecrackers in check wasn’t just for Diwali but also for “all 365 days”. They directed the state govt and other authorities to endeavour to implement timings for the bursting of firecrackers.
Article Summary: HC said it was "disturbed by comments in regard to celebrities who had participated and assisted in public cause" Justices Girish Kulkarni and Neela Gokhale said, “We would desire that in the event any goodwill message of any celebrity was taken off from the corporation’s social media"

Article Title: Up to BMC to decide whether to keep or delete clip: CM Devendra Fadnavis on actor Dia Mirza appeal row
Article Text:
CM Devendra Fadnavis

Mumbai:

TOI





Hours after Bombay HC called for restoration of actor Dia Mirza ’s video, CM Devendra Fadnavis said it was the civic body’s prerogative whether to keep or delete the clip as it manages its own social media handles.“Dia Mirza may be a good actor but she’s not some big politician from India. Hence, I don’t think this is an issue of our level,” he told reporters.BMC had not reposted the video as of Tuesday evening. A senior civic official said they were waiting for the HC order. Sources said the issue had also been taken up with the CM’s office to seek clarity on whether the video should be uploaded again.Mumbai BJP chief Ameet Satam, who was the first to raise an objection to Mirza’s post, asserted that there was no religious discrimination involved as alleged. “We have the utmost respect for the court. We will study the observations made by it and its context. There was no prayer/ petition as such specifically in context of the appeal made in the video. We, however, clarify there is no objection to any individual over one’s religion, caste and creed but only on the basis of their association with anti-India forces, anti-national elements and the ‘tukde-tukde gang’,” he toldThe opposition continued to question the civic administration and slam BJP netas, including mayor Ritu Tawde, who had called the actor “anti-Hindu” and claimed she had been kept in the dark about Mirza being roped in by the civic administration for the anti-pollution campaign along with other celebrities. “BJP turns every administration it takes over into a circus! Total clownery in BMC, where the mayor and her bosses claim they don’t know what the administration does, whenever it goes wrong! Every other mayor globally is focused on civic issues.Here the mayor’s focus has been on her car’s red beacon, residence renovation and now a citizen’s religion in a video message that was asked for by the BMC itself!” said Shiv Sena (UBT) MLA Aaditya Thackeray in a post.Kishori Pednekar, Sena (UBT)’s group leader in BMC, said Mirza’s appeal was entirely consistent with BMC’s own messaging on pollution control and environmental protection. On Tuesday, she wrote to the civic commissioner objecting to the video’s removal action and seeking appropriate administrative intervention.Waris Pathan, national spokesperson for AIMIM , echoed many opposition netas’ question: “Why was Dia Mirza singled out when others made the same appeal? The issue was pollution and public health, not politics or someone’s surname.”Sachin Sawant, national secretary of All India Congress Committee, said, “...Such distorted politics and this ideological pollution will not be tolerated. Action must be taken against those officials who have committed unconstitutional acts for BJP. If there is any integrity, Satam should apologise.”
Article Summary: BMC had not reposted the video as of Tuesday evening. A senior civic official said they were waiting for the HC order. Sources said the issue had also been taken up with the CM’s office to seek clarity on whether the video should be uploaded again.

Article Title: NCP seniors question Parth Pawar’s role at party chief Sunetra Pawar’s meeting in Mumbai
Article Text:
Discontent has arisen within the NCP over Rajya Sabha member Parth Pawar's influence in decision-making (File photo)

Parth trying to influence most decisions, say NCP seniors

Which way the wind blows?

TOI





PUNE: Discontent among NCP seniors over Rajya Sabha member Parth Pawar’s growing role in the party’s decision-making was at the core of a discussion chaired by its president and deputy chief minister Sunetra Pawar at her official residence in Mumbai on Tuesday.The meeting ended at 10.30pm and official comments by NCP state president Sunil Tatkare skirted this issue, focusing instead on “drought in several parts of the state and steps that ministers need to take post-Diwali”.“Party continues to work unitedly under Sunetra Pawar’s leadership. Some MLAs complained that they were not getting adequate funds from govt departments. They also asked if the finance portfolio would be returned to NCP,” Tatkare said.Members at the meeting questioned recent appointments to party posts as well as the functioning of Parth.“After Ajit Pawar’s death, the party unanimously selected Sunetra vahini as the next chief. However, issues started cropping up with growing interference in the party’s functioning by Parth. He has been trying to influence almost every decision without taking seniors into confidence,” a senior lawmaker from NCP told TOI.According to NCP functionaries, Sunetra had failed to take corrective measures despite their requests.A senior member of NCP told TOI, “Some appointments were recently made at the national level and in Mumbai. These appointments were not unanimous. There are talks within NCP that Parth wanted a reshuffle in the party, by bringing in some new faces and sidelining some old in the cabinet.”Following some of these appointments, prominent NCP members had met Union home minister Amit Shah in Delhi.The NCP veteran was referring to the appointments made last week when Umesh Patil replaced Brijesh Shrivastava as the party’s chief spokesperson and Zeeshan Siddique was named Mumbai unit president.Party sources said the decisions were unilaterally taken by Parth without consulting senior leaders. NCP minister Chhagan Bhujbal had publicly said that he was unaware of the appointments and learnt about them only through media reports.While the outcome of Tuesday’s meeting was yet to be determined, several changes, such as restarting the practice of holding a janta darbar at the party office in Mumbai and weekly meetings with MLAs and MLCs, have resumed. These changes, party sources said, were part of the agenda discussed at the core committee meeting on Monday.While top leadership of the party has publicly downplayed the internal friction, senior lawmakers, while speaking to TOI on condition of anonymity, confirmed that resentment has been simmering for months.The internal rift within NCP surfaced after a group of senior members met Shah in Delhi without party chief Sunetra and Parth.Those present at the meeting with Shah included Rajya Sabha MP and NCP national working president Praful Patel, state president Sunil Tatkare, ministers Bhujbal and Hasan Mushrif, former ministers Dilip Walse Patil and Dhananjay Munde, and former MLA Samir Bhujbal.Following the meeting with Shah, another round of talks happened in Mumbai on Monday before Sunetra called the meeting of the core committee at her official residence, Devgiri.One senior member who was present at the meeting with Shah told, “The discussion with the home minister was on several key issues. Based on that meeting and the core committee meeting, a four-page agenda has been finalised.” The senior NCP member denied there was any discussion on merger possibilities with Sharad Pawar-led NCP.While Sunetra gets into damage-control mode, the other faction of NCP is keeping a close watch on developments in the rival camp.While Sharad Pawar is hospitalised in Pune, NCP (SP) functionaries said they have no role in the current turmoil in NCP.A senior party functionary of NCP (SP) told TOI, “Several MLAs of NCP have met Sharad Pawar in the last couple of months but those meetings were in their personal capacity. While Sharad Pawar has made his stand clear that he will not join NDA, we doubt if any of those MLAs will leave govt and join us to be in opposition.”NCP (SP) MLA and Sharad Pawar’s grandnephew Rohit Pawar on Tuesday claimed that BJP may create a rift between Parth and Jay Pawar. Rohit alleged that BJP was attempting to sideline the sons of the deputy CM.Reacting to the meeting of NCP leaders with Amit Shah, Rohit Pawar alleged that some leaders were more concerned about safeguarding their political positions and securing ministerial berths than addressing issues concerning Ajit Pawar’s plane crash and drought relief for farmers.Warning the Pawar family about alleged attempts to take control of NCP and marginalise Sunetra and Parth, Rohit alleged that BJP and leaders close to them were pursuing a political strategy to achieve this.
Article Summary: Discontent has arisen within the NCP over Rajya Sabha member Parth Pawar's influence in decision-making. The internal rift surfaced after a group of senior members met Shah in Delhi without party chief Sunetra and Parth. NCP sources said the decisions were unilaterally taken by Parth without consulting senior leaders.

Article Title: Pubs, bars in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar to shut by 1.30am under new police rules
Article Text:
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:





City police commissioner Pravin Pawar on Tuesday issued stringent regulations for pubs, bars, permit rooms, restaurants, hotels and party lawns in the city, directing all establishments to shut by 1.30am. No fresh food or liquor orders can be accepted after 1am.The order, issued under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023, will remain in force from 12.01am on Nov 4 till midnight on Jan 2, 2027, unless withdrawn earlier.“It has come to our notice that some establishments run till the early hours with music events, DJ parties and loud sound, disturbing residents and endangering women’s safety because of unruly customers. It appears that some owners were violating mandatory norms, creating conditions for such incidents,” Pawar said.All music and entertainment programmes must end by 1.30am, while those at lawns and open spaces must stop by 10pm. Written police permission is mandatory for music events, mehfils and DJ parties. Applications for ticketed events must be submitted two weeks in advance, while details of foreign performers must be provided 15 days ahead.Customers will get 30 minutes to leave after closing.Minors below 18 are barred from permit rooms, while liquor cannot be served to anyone below 25. Establishments must verify customers’ government-issued identity cards. Dancing in seating areas is prohibited, and unruly patrons can be declared “unacceptable persons” and barred.The order also mandates CCTV surveillance, 15-day footage storage, police verification of security staff, fire audits every six months and compliance with noise norms. Intoxicated customers must not be allowed to drive. Narcotics and e-cigarettes are banned on premises.
Article Summary: All music and entertainment programmes must end by 1.30am. Dancing in seating areas is prohibited, and unruly patrons can be declared ‘unacceptable persons’ Intoxicated customers must not be allowed to drive. Narcotics and e-cigarettes are banned on premises.

Article Title: HC fines education officer Rs 25,000 for not letting teacher join despite its order
Article Text:
Aurangabad bench of Bombay HC

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:





Aurangabad bench of Bombay high court has directed Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar Zilla Parishad’s education officer (primary), Sanghratna Sarode, to pay Rs 25,000 from his own pocket to a woman teacher after finding that he failed to comply with a court order. The court also directed him to file a written unconditional apology within two weeks.A division bench of Justices Nitin Suryawanshi and Abasaheb Shinde passed the order on Oct 23 while hearing a civil application filed by teacher Surekha Thorat. The court noted that on Sept 21 it had allowed Thorat to report at Sillod headquarters until further orders. Sarode, however, directed her to report in Paithan, over 100km away.Explaining his action, Sarode told the court that since the transfer order had been issued by the chief executive officer (CEO), he sought the CEO’s approval before permitting Thorat to join in Sillod. The bench termed it a “lame excuse” and held that the officer’s stand was “erroneous and unacceptable”. The judges observed that despite “clear orders”, Sarode had “unnecessarily approached” the CEO, which amounted to acting “in utter disregard of the order of this court”.Present in court during the hearing, Sarode tendered an unconditional apology and submitted that he was a probationary officer and that it was his first mistake. Taking note of his statement, the HC cautioned him against repeating such conduct and said he “shall obey the court orders in the letter and spirit”. In-charge CEO Vasudeo Salunke, who was also directed to remain present, was discharged from the proceedings.The matter is scheduled for further hearing on Jan 15, 2027.According to the petition, Thorat joined the ZP as a teacher in Nov 2003 and was transferred to a ZP school at Golegaon in Sillod in May 2023. On July 1, she was appointed a booth-level officer by the Sillod sub-divisional officer.Thorat claimed she had applied for leave on health grounds and that the order assigning her election-related duty was not officially communicated to her. An FIR was registered against her on July 7 under Section 32 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, and she was suspended on July 16, prompting her to approach the HC.After obtaining relief from the court on Sept 21, Thorat submitted the order to the education officer’s office on Sept 23 and sent reminders on Oct 1 and Oct 7. Alleging non-compliance, she moved the civil application on Oct 16, following which the HC directed Sarode and the CEO to remain present before it on Oct 23.
Article Summary: Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar Zilla Parishad’s education officer (primary), Sanghratna Sarode, ordered to pay Rs 25,000 from his own pocket to Surekha Thorat. The court also directed him to file a written unconditional apology within two weeks.

Article Title: ​​​​Panic at Maharashtra court complexes after bomb threat emails; declared hoax after thorough check
Article Text:
Dog and bomb disposal squads conducted thorough checks after which the emails were declared hoax

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:

(With inputs from Pune, Thane, Palghar & Kolhapur)





Panic gripped courts and other establishments in parts of Maharashtra on Monday after a series of bomb threat emails triggered large-scale evacuations and security searches in several districts. Authorities later declared all the threats hoaxes after exhaustive checks found no explosives.Courts in Pune, Beed, Nanded, Parbhani, Thane, Palghar, Sangli, Satara, Solapur, Pandharpur and Ratnagiri were among those that received threatening emails warning of bomb blasts on their premises. The email also threatened to blow up a Metro station in Pune.Beed superintendent of police Navneet Kanwat said the threat email was received on the court’s official email ID. “Bomb detection and disposal squad with dog squad were rushed to the spot and launched a thorough search of the court complex and adjoining areas. No explosive items or bombs were found,” he said.Nanded SP Nilabh Rohan also confirmed that the threat turned out to be a hoax, though police acted swiftly to eliminate any possibility of sabotage.Following the alerts, court premises were evacuated and daily proceedings temporarily halted as bomb detection and disposal squad (BDDS) teams and dog squads combed the premises.Court work resumed later in the day after security clearances.At Sangli, the threat email, received around 2pm, warned of a blast at 3.11pm. “The judge informed the high court registry about the threat mail. The premises were vacated and police were called for detecting the bomb, which was not found. The court work resumed around 3.45pm,” district public prosecutor Pramod Bhokare said.The email reportedly referred to the 1984 anti-Sikh riots, spoke of avenging the deaths and claimed responsibility on behalf of a separatist group. Similar emails were received by courts in Satara, Solapur, Ratnagiri and Pandharpur, with the Pandharpur message claiming a blast would occur at 3.30pm. Fire tenders were also deployed at the Satara court complex as a precaution.“The same email also threatened to blow up the metro station. Our team also checked the metro station simultaneously but nothing was found,” said Pune police commissioner Amitesh Kumar on Monday evening.An email threat to bomb the Shivajinagar District and Sessions Court in Pune was received on the court’s official email around 2.30pm. BDDS conducted a thorough search of the court premises, but found no suspicious or bomb-like object. Pune police commissioner Amitesh Kumar said the same email also threatened to blow up a Metro station, which was checked simultaneously, but nothing was found there either.Kumar said an FIR would be registered at Shivajinagar police station.A separate threat mail to the Thane District Court sparked a major security operation after it warned of an IED attack on court premises and referred to possible attacks on Metro stations. The email also allegedly threatened a blast during singer Diljit Dosanjh ’s scheduled Nov 27 programme at Mumbai’s Mahalaxmi Racecourse and claimed an explosive device would be concealed inside an iPhone.Police evacuated judges, lawyers, litigants and court staff from both Thane court buildings, securing a 100-metre radius around the complex while BDDS teams conducted searches. No suspicious object was found.In Palghar, a threat warning of a blast at 3.11pm led to the evacuation of the district and sessions court. Cyber police have launched investigations to trace the sender and determine the origin of the coordinated threat emails, which caused disruption across multiple court complexes but resulted in no damage or injuries.
Article Summary: Courts in Pune, Beed, Nanded, Parbhani, Thane, Palghar, Sangli, Satara, Solapur, Pandharpur and Ratnagiri were among those that received threatening emails. Authorities later declared all the threats hoaxes after exhaustive checks found no explosives. Dog and bomb disposal squads conducted thorough checks after which the emails were declared hoaxes.

Article Title: No laxity will be tolerated: Abitkar gives Nanded health machinery 8-day deadline to fix services
Article Text:
Health minister Prakash Abitkar during a visit to rural Nanded on Monday

​Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:





State health minister Prakash Abitkar on Monday warned Nanded ’s public health machinery that no laxity would be tolerated, directing them to show visible improvement in attendance and healthcare services within eight days.The stern warning came after representations from former chief minister and MP Ashok Chavan , MP Dr Ajeet Gopchade, and several legislators, who flagged chronic absenteeism, vaccine and manpower shortages, lack of modern infrastructure, inadequate funding for sub-district hospitals, and demanded strict enforcement of biometric attendance and filling of vacant posts.Concluding his two-day Arogya Jansamvad Yatra 2026 in the district, Abitkar said, “No laxity will be tolerated. Act against the guilty immediately.” The statewide outreach programme is being conducted from Nov 1 to Dec 5 to strengthen public healthcare through community participation.During an interaction with private medical practitioners, the minister sought their cooperation in ensuring drought-hit citizens in Marathwada received free or affordable treatment under Ayushman Bharat-PM Jan Arogya Yojana and Mahatma Jyotirao Phule Jan Arogya Yojana.Doctors raised concerns over bogus practitioners, delayed reimbursements, technical glitches in govt portals, police action without verification after medical emergencies, and difficulties in renewing fire safety and pollution control clearances. Responding to the concerns, Abitkar assured that renewal procedures would be simplified in coordination with relevant departments. He also said no hasty legal action would be taken after an emergency without proper verification of facts and that rules would be amended wherever necessary.The minister later adopted a tougher stance during a review meeting with district health committees, taking serious note of complaints from Mukhed sub-district hospital, Sonkhed and Rahati primary health centres, and Deglur and Pimpalgaon sub-centres regarding absentee doctors, late reporting, shortages of medicines and vaccines and poor facilities. “I have ordered immediate enquiry into every absentee medical officer and employee, with a report to be submitted without delay. Action will be taken as per rules against negligent officers, with no one to be spared,” he said.Abitkar directed health committees to hold meetings every three months without fail and physically inspect hospitals to monitor staff attendance, drug availability, timely investigations, cleanliness and biomedical waste management. “Senior officers including the collector, ZP CEO, health directors and district surgeon must not sit in offices but visit health centres and verify ground reality,” he said.Announcing a new accountability mechanism, the minister said a dedicated grievance portal would be launched to allow citizens to report denial of services. “Every complaint will be tracked, responsibility fixed officer-wise and serious complaints redressed on priority,” he said.During the tour, Abitkar visited health facilities at Daregaon Tanda, Walkewadi, Dudhad, Sarsam and Himayatnagar, interacting directly with farmers, patients and healthcare workers. At drought-hit Daregaon Tanda, after inspecting crop damage, he instructed health staff to conduct door-to-door health check-ups and counselling and ensure eligible beneficiaries are not deprived of govt schemes.At Dudhad sub-centre and Sarsam PHC, he reviewed ECG and diagnostic services, while at Himayatnagar sub-district hospital he directed officials to ensure timely treatment and uninterrupted availability of essential medicines. “Poor patients must get quality treatment at the local level itself. Referrals for minor ailments must be cut, institutional deliveries must increase, pregnant women must receive timely investigations and counselling, adequate stocks essential vaccines and medicines must be maintained round the clock,” Abitkar told health authorities.
Article Summary: State health minister Prakash Abitkar on Monday warned Nanded ’s public health machinery that no laxity would be tolerated. The stern warning came after representations from former chief minister and MP Ashok Chavan, MP Dr Ajeet Gopchade, and several legislators.
